articles.title_orig: What to Expect From Best Buy's 2026 Black Friday and Cyber Monday Sales
articles.title_zh: What to Expect From Best Buy's 2026 Black Friday and Cyber Monday Sales
articles.content_orig:
For all intents and purposes, Black Friday sales are already here. There are plenty of deals out already, even though we're weeks away from the actual event. One of the reasons for that is the competition retailers have with each other to be the first to get your money. One of the retailers that is making the biggest early splash is Best Buy , confirming their entire plan for the rest of the year. Here's what you need to know.
Best Buy has announced the following events:
DoorBoosters : A Halloween sale from Oct. 30 to Nov. 1.
Early Black Friday Deals and Doorbusters: The official start of early Black Friday deals on Nov. 6. New deals will drop every Friday.
Black Friday Doorbusters and Deals : Best Buy says this will be its main sale, starting on Thursday, Nov. 19 and running until Nov. 28 with deals on "computing, gaming, home theater, wearables, and more."
Cyber Sunday and Monday : Best Buy is extending Cyber Monday to five days and says you can find deals going up to 50% off select tech.
Last-minute savings : The Christmas sale will run from Dec. 18 until Dec. 24.
You don't need to be any kind of member to shop Best Buy's Black Friday in July sale; however, it is free to sign up for a My Best Buy membership , which will get you free shipping. If you join one of their paid subscriptions (My Best Buy Plus for $49.99 per year or My Best Buy Total for $179.99 per year), you'll get faster free shipping, exclusive prices and deals, an extended 60-day return window on most products, and access to select sales, like the Member Deals Days sale that is going on right now. Paid members will also earn extra rewards from both the current sale and the upcoming Black Friday in July sale.
You can find deals on TVs, laptops, headphones, video games, electric bikes, and more. There will be new deals every week in stores, on its website, and in the Best Buy mobile app . They'll offer price matching, meaning if the price drops further during the sale (Dec. 24), they will match it and offer a refund.
Here are the best deals I've found so far. I'll be updating these deals throughout the sale, so make sure to come back and see what's new. Remember that new deals drop every day.
Best Buy price matches its own products, so if a product drops in price later, you'd get those savings too, but it does not cover any deals coming from a competitor's Black Friday sale. There are some other important exceptions you can read in more detail here .
In short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. If there’s something you want to buy, or you’re shopping for gifts, it’s a good time to look for discounts on what you need, especially tech sales, home improvement supplies, and fitness tech. Of course, if you need to save money, the best way to save is not to buy anything.
The other major retailers doing Black Friday sales are Amazon , Target , and Walmart . Currently, Amazon has many early deals, seeing their lowest prices yet. Target has some week-long deals and a Deal of the Day. Walmart will have three Black Friday and Cyber Monday shopping events. Nowadays, large retailers and small businesses compete for Cyber Monday shoppers, so you can expect practically every store to run sales through Monday, Nov. 30, 2026.
No. If you find the product you're looking for with a major discount right now, get it. It's not likely to drop any lower, but it could always run out of stock. Take advantage of price matching or guarantees instead of waiting. Remember, you can always return products later if you change your mind. For the majority of products, the deal from Black Friday will be the same one on Cyber Monday.

articles.title_orig: Four grizzly bears killed Canadian mother and daughter, authorities say
articles.title_zh: Four grizzly bears killed Canadian mother and daughter, authorities say
articles.content_orig:
Canadian wildlife officials say DNA testing linked an adult female grizzly and her three offspring to the deaths of a mother and daughter near Bella Coola, British Columbia. Investigators say the attack likely involved predatory behavior.
Four grizzly bears have been linked through DNA evidence to a deadly attack on a mother and daughter in British Columbia , prompting Canadian wildlife officers to kill all four animals, officials announced Tuesday.
The British Columbia Conservation Officer Service said forensic testing conclusively linked an adult female grizzly and her three offspring to the deaths of Jennifer Balcarras, 48, and her daughter, Selah Reed, 20, near Bella Coola.
The bears were captured over the weekend and killed in accordance with provincial human-wildlife conflict response guidelines to protect public safety, according to a Nov. 10 statement from the agency.
BODY OF MISSING HIKER DISCOVERED OFF TRAIL AS INVESTIGATORS PROBE RARE DEADLY BEAR ENCOUNTER
An image showing a photo of Jennifer Balcarras, 48, and her 20-year-old daughter Selah Reed, who were killed in a grizzly bear attack. (Facebook/Josh Kara Balcarras)
Investigators determined that the encounter likely involved predatory behavior, although officials did not elaborate on how the attack unfolded.
"This was a heartbreaking event for the families, the Nuxalk Nation and the Bella Coola community. We hope the efforts of everyone who responded, along with these findings, bring some measure of closure," said Insp. Jeff Tyre in a news briefing.
More than a dozen conservation officers participated in the response, helping recover the victims, collect evidence and locate the bears while working in difficult terrain and weather conditions.
GRIZZLY BEAR MAULS HIKER, DRAGS HIM DOZENS OF FEET ON GLACIER NATIONAL PARK TRAIL
FILE – Grizzly bear in Jasper National Park, Canada. (Getty Images/iStockphoto)
Balcarras, an art therapist, and Reed went missing after taking a walk on the Snooka West Trail near their home.
Family members contacted the Royal Canadian Mounted Police after Balcarras missed a scheduled online meet-up. Investigators found her vehicle at the trailhead before recovering her body on Nov. 2 and Reed's body on Nov. 3.
The agency said DNA testing also confirmed the four bears were not involved in a separate 2025 grizzly bear attack on a school group near Bella Coola that injured 11 people, including students and teachers.
The investigation has concluded, although officials said further analysis will examine the response and circumstances surrounding the attack.
Royal Canadian Mounted Police board, on April 10, 2024, in Edmonton, Alberta, Canada. (Artur Widak/NurPhoto via Getty Images)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
The conservation service said fatal grizzly bear attacks involving predatory behavior are rare and encouraged people traveling in bear country to leash pets, travel in groups and learn how to reduce the risk of wildlife encounters. Fox News Digital's Louis Casiano contributed to this report.
Brittany Miller is a Fox News Digital breaking news writer and former Independent reporter who graduated from Syracuse University in 2023.

articles.title_orig: After meeting Putin, U.S. envoys say Europe to join talks on ending Ukraine war
articles.title_zh: After meeting Putin, U.S. envoys say Europe to join talks on ending Ukraine war
articles.content_orig:
Russian president says he would target any foreign troops sent to Ukraine and refuses to soften territorial demands
Vladimir Putin warned US negotiators that Russia would target any foreign troops deployed to Ukraine, in a series of hardline remarks that came as the Ukrainian military faced renewed disruptions to Elon Musk’s Starlink satellite service.
During the talks at the Kremlin with the US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff on Thursday, the Russian president refused to soften his territorial demands, insisting on full control over four Ukrainian regions that Moscow claims to have annexed.
He also ruled out accepting the deployment of foreign peacekeeping troops in Ukraine , describing such a move as a “continuation of war”.
Putin’s comments appeared to severely dampen hopes that a peace deal could be within reach, after Volodymyr Zelenskyy said there was a “window of opportunity” to reach an agreement before the end of 2026.
The latest trip to Moscow by Witkoff and Kushner, who have made numerous visits to Russia, was partly aimed at securing European participation in future negotiations, according to two people familiar with the talks.
Speaking after the meeting, Witkoff confirmed that European representatives would join the next round of talks. “They’re our partners, and it’s important for them to be involved,” he told reporters as he boarded a plane leaving Moscow.
The US envoys will now travel to Dublin, Ireland, where they will meet Zelenskyy and debrief him on the Moscow meeting.
Andy Burnham, the British prime minister, said national security adviser Jonathan Powell would join the talks in Berlin.
Amid a flurry of diplomatic activity, including the recent talks in Abu Dhabi, the Kremlin appears to have succeeded in reframing negotiations over the war in Ukraine as part of a broader discussion about European security.
But Europe is wary of Russian attempts to focus discussions on a European security architecture, while Moscow continues to pound Ukraine with bombs and missiles.
The EU foreign policy chief, Kaja Kallas, told reporters: “We already have a European security architecture in place.” Kallas pointed to the cold war-era Helsinki accords and the Budapest memorandum , which guaranteed the territorial integrity of Ukraine. “The problem is that Russia is not keeping to those agreements, so right now the focus should be that Russia actually keeps to their obligations … and they don’t attack another country again.” Focusing on a European security architecture was a “distraction” without a ceasefire, she added.
Both Washington and Moscow have been urging European leaders to appoint a single representative to lead negotiations on their behalf.
“Once a representative is appointed, a chief negotiator authorised to speak on Europe’s behalf, there will be a four-way dialogue,” Putin said on Thursday.
EU leaders are due to discuss the issue of who speaks for Europe on Friday, but so far have declined to nominate one person to speak for the bloc. One EU official said the EU would be represented by its institutions when issues concerning the union were on the table, but played down any imminent appointment. They said: “Do I expect an agreement on a special representative? My answer is no, I don’t.”
Kallas suggested she – as the EU’s high representative for foreign and security policy – should represent the EU in talks, alongside António Costa, the president of the European Council.
More than 45 European leaders are meeting in Dublin for the European Political Community summit, a gathering that brings together nearly every country on the continent, apart from the leaders of Belarus and Russia.
The French president, Emmanuel Macron, played down the importance of having a single European negotiator, saying “the content determines the format”. “There is no more US support. So there [are] some mediations, fine,” he said, referring to the process led by Kushner and Witkoff. “But at the end of the day we will be the one to define and decide for our future security as Europeans.”
The German chancellor, Friedrich Merz, said it was first necessary to get Putin to the negotiating table before deciding on a European envoy. Merz said: “It’s not about individuals. What matters is that Putin is prepared to hold talks.”
Meanwhile, Zelenskyy accused Musk’s Starlink satellite service of damaging Ukraine’s ability to defend itself against Russian drone attacks, after Ukrainian military officials reported new restrictions on the system.
According to Zelenskyy, Starshield, a military version of Starlink funded by the Pentagon, has for several days been subject to speed limits of 100mph (161km/h) along the frontline and in Russian-occupied territory.
Similar restrictions last month prompted confusion over who had ordered them, with Musk and the Trump administration pointing fingers at each other before the service was partly restored.
The latest restrictions had made it harder for Ukrainian forces to intercept Russia’s increasingly sophisticated jet-powered drones, Zelenskyy said, accusing the service of “helping the Russians kill more Ukrainians and carry out more accurate strikes against Ukraine”.
Kyiv has contacted Washington to seek an explanation for the disruption, which Zelenskyy said appeared to be deliberate rather than a technical fault.

articles.title_orig: White House weighs Commerce Secretary Lutnick's ouster amid Nvidia export concerns, sources say
articles.title_zh: White House weighs Commerce Secretary Lutnick's ouster amid Nvidia export concerns, sources say
articles.content_orig:
Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick is under fire by critics asking whether his ties to Chinese companies and friendship with Nvidia's ousted CEO Jensen Huang contributed to the federal agency's lack of oversight over billions in Nvidia AI chip sales, CBS has learned.
Before President Trump nominated Lutnick to lead the Commerce Department, Lutnick was the chairman and CEO of Cantor Fitzgerald, a New York investment bank which held about $1.2 billion in Nvidia stock at the time.
Lutnick developed a warm relationship with Huang, who resigned Thursday as reports of a growing number of affairs caused new uncertainty about the world's dominant AI chipmaker. One of Huang's alleged relationships was with Alice Huang (no relation to Jensen Huang), who is believed by the U.S. to be a Chinese spy. She ran Megaspeed International, a Singapore-based company that became one of Nvidia's biggest customers for AI chips and is suspected of illegally shipping Nvidia's most advanced AI chips to Chinese entities, circumventing a U.S. ban.
As commerce secretary, Lutnick took the helm of an agency responsible for policing exports of sensitive technology to adversaries and global rivals.
One way the Commerce Department keeps this information and technology out of the hands of China and other adversaries is by putting foreign companies and individuals on its Entity List . This restricts their ability to access U.S. technology products, and inclusion on the list means that the department believes there's a risk that the entity is involved in activities that are contrary to U.S. national security or foreign policy interests.
In 2024, under the Biden administration, the Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security launched an investigation into Nvidia's chip sales to Megaspeed to determine whether they were being redirected to China. But according to The New York Times , the probe was abruptly transferred to the Department of Justice. The Justice Department would not comment about the investigation.
The Commerce Department has not added a company to the Entity List since October 2025.
Last week, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent confronted Lutnick over the Commerce Department's failure to place Megaspeed on the Entity List, Axios reported.
Chris McGuire, an expert on China and emerging technologies at the Council on Foreign Relations, said, "The real scandal here is the lack of enforcement of export controls."
He added that the Commerce Department had known for as long as a year that Megaspeed was being run by a woman who is believed by the U.S. to be a Chinese spy, "and they did nothing." The New York Times reported that about a year ago, President Trump was briefed on intelligence that suggested that Alice Huang was a Chinese asset and that she had grown close to Jensen Huang.
"Either Lutnick doesn't know how to do his job or he is protecting Huang," McGuire said.
The Commerce Department did not respond to a request for comment.
On Thursday, after Jensen Huang's resignation became public, Sen. Elizabeth Warren, the ranking Democrat on the Senate Banking Committee, called on Lutnick and his deputy, Jeffrey Kessler, to "explain why they have not closed export control loopholes." Kessler is the undersecretary who led the Commerce Department's probe into Megaspeed.
Warren urged the two to "act today to ensure our advanced technology is not fueling China's military." In March, Warren wrote to Lutnick to demand the "immediate pausing" of all export licenses of Nvidia chips destined for China.
Questions about Lutnick's own relationship with Chinese state companies have further complicated the ongoing Nvidia crisis.
A financial services firm Lutnick ran, BGC Group, had a 33% stake in a joint venture with China Credit Trust, a Chinese state-owned company whose largest shareholder is the China People's Insurance Company, another state enterprise.
Another firm he ran, Cantor Fitzgerald, is still overseen by his two eldest sons. That firm helped several Chinese companies go public in the U.S. Cantor Fitzgerald was also a key investor in Satellogic, a satellite company that is under contract with a Chinese data science company, Zhong Ke Guang Qi Space, until 2033.
His close China ties emerged as a topic at his Senate confirmation hearing last year. Senators questioned whether he could be unduly influenced by Chinese officials, and how he would safeguard U.S. technology.
Sen. Maria Cantwell, a Democrat from Washington state, grilled Lutnick on potential conflicts of interest with respect to his investments in Chinese companies, and Cantor Fitzgerald's financial interest in Tether, a cryptocurrency company with a large footprint in China.
Other senators asked about how he would safeguard U.S. technology from the Chinese Communist Party.
"How will you address different threats that we see coming from the CCP within these information and technology markets?" asked GOP Sen. Deb Fischer, of Nebraska.
Lutnick promised to be vigilant against threats from China.
"I take a very jaundiced view of China," he said in response to Fischer. "I think they only care about themselves and seek harm to us, and so we need to protect ourselves."
Before he was sworn in as commerce secretary in February 2025, Lutnick resigned from all of his corporate leadership posts, transferring his business empire to his children.
Since his tenure as commerce secretary began, Lutnick and his family's net worth doubled to $7.3 billion, thanks to his indirect stake in Tether, according to Forbes , which valued his holding in Tether at $5.4 billion. The stake, worth $1.7 billion in early 2025, has more than tripled in value.
"Can we be confident that he is looking out for the public interest?" asked Kathleen Clark, a law professor and expert on government ethics at Washington University in St. Louis. "What's going on with him raises a lot of red flags."
Lutnick's friendship with Jensen Huang may also be problematic, Clark told CBS News.
Huang met Lutnick soon after Lutnick began his term as commerce secretary, Huang told podcaster Joe Rogan last year.
"He started our conversation with, 'Jensen, this is Secretary Lutnick,'" said Huang. "'I just want to let you know that you're a national treasure. Nvidia is a national treasure. And whenever you need access to the president, the administration, you call us.'"
Huang added that every time he called the commerce secretary's office, "if I want to get something off my chest, express some concern, they're always available."
Huang also visited with President Trump. He attended a $1 million-per-person dinner at Mar-a-Lago in April 2025. At that time, Huang tried to convince Mr. Trump to lift restrictions on the company's less advanced H20 chip sales to China, according to The New York Times . Less than three months later, in July 2025, Mr. Trump lifted the restrictions. Nvidia's most advanced chip, the Blackwell, still cannot be sold directly to China.
In July 2025, Lutnick posted a photo to Instagram showing Huang in his trademark black leather jacket standing in the Oval Office next to Mr. Trump, who was seated at his desk. Lutnick is also in the photo along with other visitors.
"Great to meet in the Oval Office with Jensen Huang on the very day Nvidia crossed $4 trillion in market cap," the post said.

articles.title_orig: Newsom blasts Trump’s climate retreat as giving China an edge
articles.title_zh: Newsom blasts Trump’s climate retreat as giving China an edge
articles.content_orig:
Gov. Gavin Newsom blasted President Trump’s retreat from the fight against climate change, casting it as a global embarrassment and a squandered opportunity to make domestic manufacturing gains.
“China is cleaning our clock,” Newsom said on the sidelines of the United Nations-backed climate negotiations in Antalya, Turkey. “It’s not just about environmental policy. It’s about influence, it’s about supply chains, it’s about investment. As we walk off the international stage, they’re stepping in, and they’re also stepping in with this new technology.”
Newsom, a potential Democratic contender for the U.S. presidency in 2028, was joined by a phalanx of other governors and mayors at the COP31 summit Thursday. Their presence at the talks was a show of force meant to illustrate the work that cities and states are still doing to decarbonize following the Trump administration’s rollback of emission-limiting regulations and withdrawal from the Paris Agreement.
The U.S. government didn’t send an official delegation to the high-level talks, which have brought together nearly 200 countries. Instead, the country was represented unofficially by other U.S. officials. On Thursday, the group included U.S. Sen. Sheldon Whitehouse of Rhode Island, Minnesota Gov. Tim Walz, New Mexico Gov. Michelle Lujan Grisham and a number of mayors. A coalition of some 19 U.S. House representatives also are set to participate later this week.
Newsom, however, was by far the most visible representative of the U.S., mobbed by dozens of reporters, activists and onlookers as he inched slowly through the venue Thursday, occasionally stopping for selfies and winning the same kind of acclaim showered earlier in the week on Brazil’s newly reelected President Lula da Silva. “We love you, Governor Newsom,” shouted one observer. “You must be president!” yelled another.
U.S. representatives at the climate talks said they were buoyed by the U.S. midterm elections last week, which ushered Democrats into control of the House and Senate as well as a majority of state governorships.
“We’re doing all of this in our states with no help from Washington,” Walz said, adding that Democratic control of Congress could help facilitate those efforts. Under Trump, the federal government has been “throwing barriers into place,” he said, but “it’ll be very difficult for them to do that now.”
Newsom also said he felt “renewed optimism from the midterms” but remained concerned about two more years of environmental policy under Trump. Democrats can wield fresh power to mitigate “the damage,” he said, but can only go so far.
“Trump’s head is in sand soaked with oil. He’s a wholly-owned subsidiary of big oil and we have been on the receiving end of some of the most aggressive assaults on our climate leadership in our generation,” Newsom said.
During Trump’s second term, the administration has pulled back a host of Biden-era regulations, including a mix of mandates and subsidies that encouraged electric vehicles. That’s imperiling American competitiveness, Newsom said.
“I worry about American automobile manufacturers surviving a decade from now,” Newsom said. “If you care about the future of American manufacturing and of automobile manufacturing, you should care about this issue. And so that’s the message I’m communicating here in the absence of one damn representative from the federal government. We are a footnote yet again at COP and that is a disgrace.”
Leaders of cities and states representing more than 60% of the U.S. economy have used the summit to pledge they’d keep forging forward on climate —including by formally collaborating with United Nations officials in tracking the country’s greenhouse gas emissions.
That pledge came in a joint statement from America Is All In, the U.S. Climate Alliance and Climate Mayors initiatives. Collectively, they represent 24 governors with constituents making up 55% of the U.S. population as well as 350 mayors across 47 states.
The two-week COP31 summit is meant to galvanize a worldwide shift away from fossil fuels, an embrace of more emission-free renewable alternatives and additional conservation efforts. The alliances of state and local leaders committed to working with the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, the treaty and institution undergirding the 2015 Paris accord, without support from the U.S. government. Under a formal process kicked off this year, the U.S. is set to officially exit the UNFCCC next February.
The new effort by cities, states and other leaders will involve elevating data on U.S. progress toward decarbonization by midcentury and ensuring engagement in a “global stocktake” exercise meant to assess how the world is doing in meeting its climate goals. A first global stocktake culminated in 2023 with a recognition the world was badly off track its key temperature target, prompting a pledge at COP29 in Dubai to transition away from fossil fuels. Initial discussions are underway in Turkey on the second stocktake set to conclude in 2028.
UN Secretary-General António Guterres told Bloomberg TV Thursday that he welcomed U.S. subnational action on climate. “The U.S. is not the U.S. government,” he said. “We see the private sector in the U.S. clearly more and more investing in renewables, and we see more and more governors and more and more mayors totally committed to that. And I hope that the U.S. as a whole will become again an important part.”
U.S. state-level policy, market forces and falling technology costs can reduce carbon dioxide emissions by as much as 46% below 2005 levels by 2035, according to a report from America Is All In and the University of Maryland Center for Global Sustainability.

articles.title_orig: Cramer says Jensen Huang betrayed Nvidia shareholders. How to pick up the pieces
articles.title_zh: Cramer says Jensen Huang betrayed Nvidia shareholders. How to pick up the pieces
articles.content_orig:
CNBC's Jim Cramer criticized former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang on Thursday for putting the chipmaker's future at risk.
"Did he betray you, the shareholders?" Cramer asked. "Yes. End of story."
Huang resigned Thursday morning following reports of an affair with an Nvidia executive who reported to him. Hours later, Reuters reported that he had an "intimate relationship" with a second employee. These revelations came days after Huang admitted to an affair with an executive at a Singapore-based cloud computing company whom U.S. intelligence agencies suspect of spying for China. Longtime CFO Colette Kress was named interim CEO of Nvidia. Cramer said Huang's departure was necessary to protect Nvidia from further fallout.
Shares ended Thursday down more than 4%, but at its lows of the morning, the stock was off over 14%. The decline in Thursday's session brings Nvidia's losses this year to 12%.
While questions remain about what comes next for the AI chipmaker, Cramer argued that Nvidia's future extends beyond the executive who helped build it into one of the world's most valuable companies. "There won't be a better Nvidia, just a different one [without Huang]," Cramer said, envisioning a company that is better organized and more disciplined about its investments.
Under Huang, Nvidia built an extensive equity investment portfolio that included a $5 billion investment in Intel in 2025 and a $2 billion investment in AI cloud provider CoreWeave earlier this year. The investments, and many others, were part of Huang's strategy to strengthen Nvidia's position across the AI industry.
During the CNBC Investing Club's Morning Meeting livestream Thursday, Cramer recalled urging Kress to reduce the company's stakes in Intel and CoreWeave, only to be told that Huang preferred to maintain them. Cramer suggested that new leadership could take a more disciplined approach to capital allocation, potentially cashing in on some of those investments and returning the proceeds to shareholders through even bigger stock buybacks.
Cramer expressed confidence in Kress, praising her deep understanding of Nvidia's operations and financials. He argued that the longtime finance chief is well positioned to provide stability as the company navigates the investigations surrounding Huang, which stretch from the boardroom to Washington, D.C.
Nvidia didn't respond to CNBC's request for comment on Cramer's remarks. Heller, the crisis PR firm Huang reportedly hired as early as last year, did not respond to CNBC's request for comment.
Going forward, Nvidia's underlying business remains strong, Cramer said, pointing to its substantial cash reserves and expectations for a robust earnings report Tuesday evening. But he cautioned that even strong quarterly results might not be enough to reassure investors during this time of lingering uncertainty.
Investigations into Huang's conduct and possible violations of U.S. chip export restrictions could result in sanctions that hurt Nvidia's international business. Meanwhile, competitors, including Advanced Micro Devices , are making progress with their own AI chips, potentially threatening Nvidia's market dominance. AMD shares surged almost 6% on Thursday, extending their winning streak to five straight sessions.
Those risks have prompted Cramer to take a more cautious approach to Nvidia stock , particularly after the substantial gains shares have delivered over the years for Cramer's Charitable Trust , the portfolio of 32 stocks managed by the Club. On Tuesday, as Huang's future at Nvidia looked more and more in doubt, the Club downgraded Nvidia to a hold-equivalent rating.
"Don't ever turn a successful investment into an unsuccessful trade," he said, urging longtime shareholders sitting on big gains to consider taking some profits. "You don't want to give up all of your gains if the stock falls further. It fell further today after many of the analysts jumped ship and downgraded the stock from buy to hold. There could be more ahead."
At the same time, Cramer cautioned against giving up on Nvidia altogether, pointing to the company's extensive engineering expertise and multiyear product roadmap as reasons to believe it can continue competing at the forefront of AI without Huang.
The "Mad Money" host also drew parallels to Apple's leadership transition from Steve Jobs to Tim Cook , suggesting that Nvidia could benefit from a similarly capable successor who brings a different management style without sacrificing the company's technological edge.

According to Bloomberg , the US Attorney's Office out of Manhattan is looking into the matter.
The Department of Justice is already investigating a chip-smuggling campaign related to Huang and her former company, the Singapore-based Megaspeed.
Huang is the woman who allegedly had an affair with former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang . She is also suspected of spying for the Chinese government.

The company has faced controversy in the past.
In 2020, the Securities and Exchange Commission charged Super Micro with "widespread accounting violations." The company settled the charges after agreeing to pay a $17.5 million civil penalty.
In 2024, short-selling organization Hindenburg Research issued a report calling Super Micro's accounting into question.
The company's accounting firm EY subsequently resigned over concerns about transparency and internal controls over financial reporting.
In March of this year, the United States Attorney's Office for the Southern District of New York unsealed an indictment alleging that Super Micro senior vice president of business development and member of the board of directors Yih-Shyan "Wally" Liaw and two others established a scheme to smuggle servers into China .

articles.title_orig: EXCLUSIVE: Kalshi says it ended Donald Trump Jr's advisory contract over Polymarket conflict
articles.title_zh: EXCLUSIVE: Kalshi says it ended Donald Trump Jr's advisory contract over Polymarket conflict
articles.content_orig:
Kalshi announces ‘mutual decision’ as Democrats say they plan to investigate Trump family’s investments
Donald Trump Jr is no longer a paid adviser for Kalshi, the prediction market company said Thursday.
Kalshi described it as a mutual business decision between the two parties that followed a decision by Trump Jr’s investment firm, 1789 Capital, to increase its investment in Kalshi’s biggest competitor Polymarket.
But the announcement comes a week after Democrats were able to take control of both the House and Senate in the midterm elections.
Democrats have said they planned to investigate the Trump family’s investments, including their business relationships with both prediction markets.
“We have mutually agreed to end Don’s advisory role after his firm’s significant investment in a competitor this past summer,” said Dani Lever, a spokesperson for Kalshi. “We are grateful for his contributions in helping us market Kalshi to more customers.”
The president’s eldest son became a paid “strategic adviser” for Kalshi shortly after President Trump was sworn into office for his second term in January 2025 and has been an investor in Polymarket since August 2025. Both companies have seen their popularity and use jump significantly in the past two years.
At the same time, both companies have received favorable treatment from the White House. The Commodity Futures Trading Commission has backed the industry’s efforts to expand their products nationwide, including allowing their customers to trade sports-related contracts.
Both companies have adamantly denied that the financial relationship between Polymarket, Kalshi and the Trumps played any role in how the industry has been regulated under this administration.
1789 Capital increased its investment in Polymarket this past August, as part of Polymarket’s latest fundraising round. It was this investment that started the conversation about ending Trump Jr’s advisory role with Kalshi.

articles.title_orig: What’s a Honey Trap? The spy tactic that helped topple Jensen Huang
articles.title_zh: What’s a Honey Trap? The spy tactic that helped topple Jensen Huang
articles.content_orig:
A screengrab from CTI video footage obtained November 9, 2026 shows a woman identified by Reuters as Alice Huang after comparison with a photograph obtained separately, attending a dinner with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang (in black) at a restaurant in Taipei, Taiwan on May 22, 2025. CTI via Reuters hide caption
One of the world's oldest spy tactics appears to have helped topple one of the world's richest men. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned Thursday amid revelations that he had an affair with a female client that U.S. intelligence identified as a Chinese spy, according to the New York Times.
NPR has not independently confirmed the reporting by the Times, which said Huang also had an unrelated affair with a company executive who reported to him. The Chinese government has called the accusation of spying, "nothing but smears against China."
Using a romantic relationship to gather intelligence from foreigners – known as a honey trap – has a long history in China and beyond. The Chinese Ministry of State Security, the country's main civilian intelligence agency, routinely tries to recruit women and occasionally men for honey traps, according to former CIA officers and other U.S. officials familiar with Chinese spy craft.
Some target businessmen for industrial espionage or to gain insights into the economic and political strategy of foreign governments. Peter Mattis , a former CIA counter-intelligence analyst, said honey traps also serve as influence operations with spies trying to gain enough trust to shape the target's thinking about China.
"The biggest thing here that we should pay attention to is that the Ministry of State Security celebrates a tradition of getting inside the enemy's decision-making," said Mattis, president of the Jamestown Foundation , a national security think tank in Washington, D.C., that focuses on America's geopolitical rivals.
Nicholas Eftimiades , who spent more than 34 years with the CIA and Defense Intelligence Agency and now teaches at Penn State, said the honey trap is just one tactic among many that use ordinary Chinese citizens to gather information at home and abroad.
"Unlike the CIA, or MI6 or any of the other Western services, China has a 'whole of society approach,'" said Eftimiades, the author of Chinese Intelligence Operations: An Analysis of the People's Republic of China's Intelligence Services. "Chinese law supports this. The National Intelligence Law of 2017 requires citizens to cooperate with intelligence collection efforts."
The Chinese government has employed honey traps in the United States and elsewhere in the West. In the 2010s, Christine Fang worked as a political fundraiser in California where she developed a physical relationship with Democrat Rep. Eric Swalwell before and after he became a congressman.
The FBI warned Swalwell they thought Fang was a spy. He denied doing anything wrong and she fled back to China.
In the 1980s and 1990s, the FBI paid Katrina Leung – a Los Angeles businesswoman – $1.7 million over 18 years to spy on China. However, Leung had affairs with two FBI agents and the bureau later determined she was a double-agent.
The most remarkable honey trap case dates to the 1960s, when a young French diplomat began a nearly two-decade affair with a male Peking opera performer, whom he thought was a woman. The story inspired the play and movie, M Butterfly .
The woman implicated in the Nvidia case, Alice Huang, is a Chinese businesswoman whose company, Megaspeed, was a major buyer of advanced chips from Nvidia. The Times reported the U.S. had her under surveillance and learned of her connections to Chinese state security through her communications.
The logo of data center company Megaspeed International is pictured at its office in the Ocean Financial Centre in Singapore on November 10, 2026. The woman accused of spying for China during an affair with Jensen Huang, head of US artificial intelligence chip titan Nvidia, has been named in media reports as tech executive Alice Huang, who has reportedly been a top figure at Singapore-based company. Taryn Ng/AFP via Getty Images hide caption
Desmond Shum, a Hong Kong businessman and former China insider, says Alice Huang doesn't fit the usual profile in these cases. She appears to be what the Chinese call a "white glove" – or front-person for multi-billion-dollar commercial deals, which Shum says could have insulated her from the Ministry of State Security.
Shum doesn't think Alice Huang is a professional spy, pointing out that she hasn't been discreet on social media, posting photos from her visits to luxurious country clubs and fancy foreign destinations.
"A spy wouldn't do that," Shum told NPR from his home in the United Kingdom.
Isaac Stone Fish , a former reporter in China who runs Strategy Risks, a China-focused business intelligence firm, says the Ministry of State Security – or MSS – could have approached Alice Huang after it learned of her affair with the Nvidia head.
"One imagines that every time a Chinese person enters into a romantic relationship with a very, very powerful American, MSS notices that," Stone Fish said.
Honey traps are a staple of spy novel and movie plots, including the Netflix series, Black Doves , The Americans on FX, Apple TV's Slow Horses as well as James Bond films, such as From Russia with Love .
In reality, when Chinese state security approaches women for these operations, it's embarrassing and humiliating. The tactic perpetuates racist, sexist stereotypes while casting suspicion on the vast majority of Chinese people, who have nothing to do with intelligence gathering.
In addition to China, many intelligence services have engaged in honey traps. The Russians historically used sex workers for blackmail and leverage. During the Cold-War, East Germany sent well-educated and well-mannered male spies – known as Romeos – to West Germany.
Mossad, the Israeli intelligence service, used honey traps from the 1950s into the 1970s in countries such as Egypt, Iraq and Iran. But investigative reporter Yossi Melman, who's written many books on Israeli intelligence, says the practice has dwindled as cyber spying and digital traps have proven more efficient.
The U.S. used sexual entrapment against the Soviets, but several former officials said the Americans now prefer to appeal to people on ideological grounds and provide financial carrots, such as money for college tuition or health care for a sick family member.
Even though countries repeatedly warn businessmen and government officials about the tell-tale signs of a honey trap, ego and vanity remain human weaknesses and men continue to succumb, said Eftimiades.
"Welcome to the male of the species," he said. "Is everyone aware of this? Yes. Does everyone think it'll happen to them? No. And, you know, and it happens all the time."

articles.title_orig: What to Know About the Bomb Threats Rattling Europe
articles.title_zh: What to Know About the Bomb Threats Rattling Europe
articles.content_orig:
Italy’s government said on Thursday that public buildings facing bomb scares should not be evacuated unless there was genuine evidence of danger, as hoax threats targeting schools, flights and other places continued to rattle daily life around Europe.
A day after hoax bomb threats were emailed to over 6,000 schools in Italy, prompting hundreds to be evacuated, the Italian government said in a statement that buildings that receive such security alerts should not empty out “unless there is concrete evidence, other than a simple mass email, suggesting a danger exists.”
It is unclear who is behind the hoax threats, which have also affected Ireland, France, Spain, Poland and other countries, and how they might be connected. But European officials have characterized them as part of a coordinated campaign to sow confusion across the continent.
“These messages are not meant to inflict harm; they are meant to spread fear,” Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni of Italy said in a statement on Wednesday. “Above all, those who write them want our fear, wasted days, mistrust and chaos.”
Officials have emphasized that the extent of the threats remains limited. The number of flights affected this month, for example, was a fraction of the tens of thousands that operate daily in Europe. When another wave of emails threatened hundreds of Italian schools on Thursday, only a handful were evacuated, according to ANSA , Italy’s main news agency.
But anxiety is running high on the continent , where hybrid warfare attacks and intimidation tactics have shaken air travel and other industries in recent months as Russia’s war against Ukraine spills over its borders .

articles.title_orig: US intel isn’t sure if businesswoman spied on Nvidia for China, doesn’t mean she wasn’t a risk, sources say
articles.title_zh: US intel isn’t sure if businesswoman spied on Nvidia for China, doesn’t mean she wasn’t a risk, sources say
articles.content_orig:
The US intelligence community is still working to understand the relationship between a Chinese businesswoman who had an affair with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and the Chinese government, with multiple sources telling CNN that the intelligence collected on her to date does not prove that she was acting as a spy for Beijing.
There is disagreement among US officials about the strength of the evidence that Alice Huang was recruited by the Chinese Ministry of State Security (MSS), the Chinese equivalent of the CIA, to spy on Jensen Huang — and, by extension, on US policymakers.
The FBI has been investigating Huang’s affair for at least a year. But Attorney General Todd Blanche said on Thursday that there are still “no conclusions reached by the Department of Justice, or by me, or by [FBI] Director Patel around who she is or is not.” President Donald Trump also hedged Thursday on whether the US had determined she was a spy, when commentator Stephen A. Smith asked whether Huang was right to have stepped down as CEO.
“Well, the big thing is, was the woman a spy? And I don’t know if that’s been determined yet,” Trump said. “But if the woman was a spy, yes. If the woman was not a spy, perhaps it would be different.”
Some officials at the Office of the Director of National Intelligence, including those close to director Jay Clayton, have framed the characterization of Alice Huang as a Chinese spy as not entirely accurate and over-torqued, sources said. And officials at the CIA also are not yet convinced that the intelligence collection on Huang to date, including intercepted communications, proves she was knowingly funneling information back to Beijing, a source told CNN.
Still, some Trump officials told CNN that it strains credulity to believe that she was not acting as an agent of the Chinese government — simply by virtue of the fact that she is a successful Chinese businesswoman working with one of America’s most powerful companies .
Under Chinese national security law, Chinese citizens can be compelled to help gather intelligence on behalf of the Chinese Communist Party. Even if she had not done so yet, given her access to Huang — and by extension, to  Trump — some officials believe she posed a clear counterintelligence risk. But to others, the fixation on Huang’s relationship to the Chinese government has obscured broader questions around the US government’s failure to crack down on the diversion to China of sophisticated technology vital to the AI race.
Alice Huang’s Singapore-based company Megaspeed is a major purchaser of NVIDIA chips. The Department of Justice and the Commerce Department began an investigation into the firm in 2024 — part of a broader probe into an ecosystem of foreign shell companies suspected of diverting restricted Nvidia chips to China, a person briefed on the investigation said.
There are now questions brewing inside the White House over why the Commerce Department did not put Megaspeed on the so-called “entity list,” which restricts trade with companies that may pose a risk to US national security or foreign policy interests — at least while the investigation was ongoing, according to a person familiar.
“An intelligence operation wasn’t necessary to achieve that result,” a former Commerce Department official told CNN, noting that Jensen Huang has publicly advocated for the US to sell more chips to China. The fact that chips might be diverted to China through Megaspeed was, theoretically, a place where China’s interest already coincided with Nvidia’s — and “a regulatory loophole” already allowed it, the former Commerce official added.
Jensen Huang resigned from Nvidia on Wednesday, following days of reports that he had had an affair with a suspected Chinese intelligence asset. Reports also emerged on Wednesday night that he separately had an affair with a subordinate at Nvidia.
Democratic Rep. Jim Himes, the ranking member of the House Intelligence Committee, told POLITICO Thursday that he left a classified briefing with senior intelligence officials earlier this week unsure of the nature of Huang’s relationship with the Chinese government.
“What’s the relationship with Alice Huang and the Chinese, and what do we know about what influence or information was traded? Because today, at least, I don’t know,” Himes said.
Last year, when US intelligence officials first learned of the relationship between Huang and Alice Huang, officials across the government immediately wanted to know more — and some began sounding the alarm.
Secretary of State and National Security Adviser Marco Rubio warned in a memo in the spring about Jensen’s relationship with Huang, one source told CNN. But it is unclear how detailed the memo got on how much information Huang was or was not sharing with the Chinese government. Rubio briefed Trump on Jensen Huang and his relationship with Alice Huang aboard Air Force One en route to China in May.
The briefing occurred before Jensen Huang joined Trump in Alaska for the final leg of the trip, a source briefed on the matter told CNN.
Different agencies have continued conducting their own reviews of the intelligence, sources said. One particularly alarming development occurred when US intelligence  obtained communications that appeared to indicate someone with close access to Jensen Huang and Nvidia was the source of information that ended up in Chinese intelligence streams, a person familiar with the investigation told CNN.
The FBI, which is conducting the primary counterintelligence investigation, told lawmakers last year that it was particularly suspicious of Alice Huang’s seemingly overnight career pivot from Chinese State television journalist to businesswoman with an unusually large amount of purchasing power in the Chinese economy, one of the sources said.
That, paired with her close relationship to the then-Nvidia CEO has continued to raise red flags inside the bureau, where the counterintelligence probe remains ongoing, according to multiple sources familiar with the matter.
Definitively linking suspicious behavior by Chinese nationals interacting with the United States to a state-directed spying campaign remains a perennial problem for counterintelligence officials trying to defend against Chinese espionage. It is notoriously difficult to collect intelligence on China, and China routinely compels its private citizens to do its bidding overseas.
When it comes to Chinese spying, the threat is in the eye of the beholder — some officials think the fears are overblown, other officials see a Chinese spy in every encounter.
“A lot of these people are guilty of just being Chinese,” said a former senior counterintelligence official.
But Joshua Hodges, a commissioner on the US-China Economic and Security Review Commission, which investigates how US-China trade and economic ties affect American national security, said that “we’ve seen repeatedly the Chinese are incredibly adept at using people both wittingly and unwittingly.”
“Ultimately, what we typically see is those people, at a certain point in time, recognize that they know who they’re working for and they know the ends that they’re working towards,” he told CNN.
Hodges, who served on the National Security Council in Trump’s first term, noted Huang’s past rhetoric denouncing the phrase “China hawks” as “a badge of shame.”
“That clearly is directed to make people stop talking about the topic,” Hodges said. “You’ve got the biggest, one of the biggest, CEOs in the world attacking people for speaking out about something they care about — that clearly only benefits one country.”
CNN’s Kristen Holmes and Alejandra Jaramillo contributed to this report.

articles.title_orig: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns in wake of affair with woman suspected of spying for China
articles.title_zh: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns in wake of affair with woman suspected of spying for China
articles.content_orig:
Jensen Huang resigned as CEO of AI tech giant Nvidia effective immediately following a scandal involving an alleged spy, the company's board of directors announced Thursday.
The decision came amid an investigation into Huang's affair with a woman U.S. intelligence agencies suspect was spying for China. President Trump said this week the FBI is investigating romantic and business ties between Huang and suspected Chinese spy Alice Huang. The two aren't related.
Nvidia's board had been preparing to oust Huang , two sources familiar with the matter confirmed to CBS News on Wednesday night, plans that were first reported by the Wall Street Journal.
Huang's ouster also follows a New York Times report Wednesday that five employees at Nvidia came forward alleging Huang was romantically involved with a subordinate, Kimberly Powell, Nvidia's vice president of healthcare.
The Times also reported Huang and Powell, who are both married to other people, were caught on video being affectionate at a conference in March, according to two Nvidia employees. The Times has not seen the video and CBS News has not verified the report.
After Huang's resignation was announced Thursday, the Reuters news agency reported that Huang also had an intimate relationship with a second employee, according to two people familiar with the matter. The agency only identified the employee as a woman.
The company's interim CEO will be Colette Kress, who is currently Nvidia's chief financial officer and will continue in that role.
"The Board has full confidence in Colette and the leadership team, and we expect the company's operations, customer commitments and product roadmap to continue without interruption," Harvey Jones, who was announced as the company's first board chair, said in a statement.
Kress has been Nvidia's CFO since she joined the company in 2013. She previously worked in finance roles at tech companies like Cisco and Microsoft for nearly 25 years.
Nvidia was co-founded by Huang in 1993. It became one of the most valuable companies in the world by designing the powerful semiconductors that fuel many of the world's leading AI firms, making its technology highly sensitive and subject to export controls limiting sales to China.
Nvidia's stock plunged as news emerged of the company's turmoil, potentially erasing almost $500 billion in value. In Thursday's trading, the stock price closed down 4.3% at $166.19.
Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, was an executive at Megaspeed International , a Singapore-based data center company whose website touts its partnership with Nvidia.
Megaspeed grew with the help of access to Nvidia's restricted AI computer chips. According to U.S. investigators, Alice Huang was able to gain access to 240,000 chips that were banned from being exported to China. Megaspeed is under investigation in the U.S. and Singapore for allegedly smuggling those chips into China.
In Washington, top Democrats on Capitol Hill have expressed concerns over whether Jensen Huang's ties to Alice Huang may have compromised U.S. national security.
Following Jensen Huang's resignation, Democratic Sen. Elizabeth Warren of Massachusetts said his departure doesn't absolve him or the company from the scandal.
"Mr. Huang, NVIDIA executives, and NVIDIA's board of directors still owe Congress answers about the company's compliance with U.S. export controls," Warren said in a statement.
Before Huang resigned, Dan Ives, partner and senior managing director at Yorkville Ives & Co., told CBS News the departure could help China in the competition between Beijing and the U.S.
"With him out as CEO, China could significantly narrow the gap versus the U.S.," Ives said. He added: "The problem now is that there's no replacement for Jensen. It's a black eye moment for him, for Nvidia, and actually the U.S. tech industry. I'd say it's dark day for, you know, U.S. technology."
Following Thursday morning's announcement, Mr. Trump said on his Truth Social platform that there was "only one man" who could replace Huang: former Apple CEO Tim Cook .
Mr. Trump had a close relationship with Huang, who has attended AI-focused White House events and traveled with Mr. Trump to China. Late last year, Mr. Trump granted Nvidia the right to sell advanced H200 chips to "approved customers" in China, with the U.S. government getting a 25% cut — a major coup for Huang, who has long sought to sell more technology to the Chinese market. The deal did not cover Nvidia's even more advanced Blackwell and Rubin systems.
In a radio interview Thursday, Mr. Trump brought up that he gave Huang a National Medal of Science earlier this year. "What a horrible thing that is," he said of the situation involving Huang, adding, "That's so sad to see that happen."
The president also said in an interview: "What a horrible thing that is
In a statement accompanying her appointment as interim CEO, Kress said that the company's focus will be on "serving our customers, partners, developers and shareholders."
"NVIDIA's strength has always come from its people, and together with our leadership team, I am committed to building on the extraordinary foundation Jensen created over the last 33 years," Kress said.
The board said it will be conducting a search for a permanent CEO and will consider internal and external candidates.
Jennifer  Jacobs , Jo Ling  Kent , Aimee  Picchi and Isabel  Vincent contributed to this report.

articles.title_orig: Israeli strike on Gaza’s Nasser Hospital kills at least six people, officials say
articles.title_zh: Israeli strike on Gaza’s Nasser Hospital kills at least six people, officials say
articles.content_orig:
An Israeli airstrike on a hospital in southern Gaza overnight killed at least six people, the Health Ministry in the Palestinian enclave said Thursday.
The strike hit a surgery building at Nasser Hospital, with medical staff and patients among those killed, including a surgeon and a 13-year-old boy, health officials said. The Israeli military said it was targeting a Hamas commander and other militants.
The strike — the latest despite an ongoing U.S.-backed ceasefire — shattered ceilings and left debris strewn across wards inside the hospital, which is one of the few functioning medical facilities left in Gaza after the destruction of Israel’s yearslong military assault.
Palestinian surgeon Dr. Rizk Abu Shaira was among those killed, the Health Ministry said. He was featured in the 2026 documentary “American Doctor,” which followed three American doctors helping to provide medical care in Gaza.
An array of munitions debris was displayed at the hospital site as media visited on Thursday. Two munitions experts said an image supplied to NBC News appeared to show debris from a GBU-39 Small Diameter Bomb. The U.S. is known to supply Israel with GBU-39 munitions, which are produced by Boeing in the United States and sold to a number of countries.
The IDF and Pentagon did not immediately respond to a request for comment on whether U.S.-manufactured munitions were used in the strike. While the image was captured at Nasser Hospital following the strike, NBC News is not able to independently confirm that they were the munitions used in the attack or how they came to be displayed there.
Justin Bronk, a senior research fellow for airpower and technology in the military sciences at the Royal United Services Institute, a think tank based in London, said he made that determination based on the “wing section visible,” adding that the GBU-39 “is a U.S. supplied weapon.”
Brian Castner, a crisis researcher at Amnesty International, also identified the munitions as belonging to a GBU-39, adding that Israel has used the bomb “in many strikes in Gaza.”
Sam Lair, a fellow at the Foreign Policy Research Institute who manages and conducts investigations into nuclear and missile programs, said NBC News’ imagery appeared inconclusive, but “the wings, tail actuation system, lugs, and warhead” shown in other photos appear to match “a GBU-39 series small diameter bomb.”
“It looks to be some kind of glide bomb or cruise missile, and the English on the frame suggests it could be U.S.-origin, but I don’t see anything conclusive,” he said.
Dr. Ayman Abu Obeid, head of the surgery department at Nasser Hospital, said there was no “notice, warning or anything” before the hospital was attacked. “Suddenly, there was fire and shelling and walls were brought down instantly,” he said.
He said he was not aware of any “resistance fighters or combatants present — only a medical team treating patients.”
NBC News also spoke with two surgeons who travelled to Gaza from the U.K. earlier this month to assist with medical care, and were said were in the hospital when the missile struck.
Both Dr. Goher Rahbour, a consultant general and colorectal surgeon, and Dr. Stephan Verborg, a limb reconstruction surgeon, said they were also not aware of any warning from the Israeli military before the strike, which hit the hospital shortly after midnight.
“I heard the impact and I felt the explosion because the whole hospital shook,” Verborg said in a phone interview Thursday. He said he was about 15 to 20 meters away from the point of impact, adding: “You could smell the smoke. You could see the dust.”
Rahbour said he had been operating with Abu Shaira, whom he described as a “lovely” and “affable” person, earlier that day. He said they had been laughing and joking together Wednesday evening in the hours just before the Palestinian surgeon was killed.
Both doctors had traveled to Gaza early this month through the organization IDEALS, a U.K. charity seeking to provide sustainable humanitarian aid to regions affected by conflict or natural disasters. They said they had not seen any indication of a Hamas presence in the hospital.
Tributes were paid to Abu Shaira. “Dr. Rizq was at the hospital during the entire war,” Dr. Mohammed Zaqout, director general of the Health Ministry in Gaza, could be seen telling a crowd of mourners, surrounding a body covered in a shroud, in a video captured for NBC News on Thursday. “He didn’t abandon his duties for even one day.”
Nasser Hospital said a 13-year-old boy, identified as Jihad Naeem Muhammad Abu Tilikh, was also among those killed.
The Israeli military and the Israel Security Agency said they struck a senior Hamas member, along with other militants, who they said had “advanced” attacks from the hospital in the southern Gaza Strip overnight. In a later statement, they identified the senior member as Muhammad Abu Ismail, who they said served as the commander of Hamas’ Khan Younis Brigade and had also been responsible for holding hostages in Gaza.
The IDF and ISA said Hamas had “established a presence within the hospital complex and used it as a command center” and stored weapons and conducted interrogations and torture from within the medical complex.
The IDF claimed the hospital’s second floor “serves as a Hamas military HQ, where civilians are not permitted to enter,” alleging that “dozens of hostages were held captive” there earlier in the war. It shared photos of weapons alleged to have been found within the complex.
The IDF and ISA said steps had been taken to “mitigate harm to civilians, including the use of precision munitions and aerial surveillance.” They also later said “advance warnings were issued to the population.” The IDF said it was looking into reports that medical workers,  including Abu Shaira, and patients were killed.
One woman, Tahani Ibrahim Abu Anza, said her brother, Khaled Abu Anza, was killed in the strike, with Nasser Hospital separately confirming his death.
A number of media outlets, including Israeli media outlet Ynet , reported that a commander in Hamas’ Khan Younis Brigade of that same name was killed in the strike. Asked to confirm that and whether he was directly targeted, the IDF said it would get back on the matter.
Tahani Ibrahim Abu Anza did not directly identify her brother, 53, as a Hamas member, but said she believed he was targeted. He had been at the hospital for physical therapy after undergoing surgery, she said.
“He did not come to the hospital to engage in combat or resistance. He came for medical treatment,” she said.
Hamas condemned the allegations that it was using the hospital for military operations as “lies of the criminal enemy” and called the attack a “war crime.”
Hospitals have protected status under international law, but they have been heavily targeted under Israel’s yearslong offensive in Gaza. The Israeli military has repeatedly accused Hamas of operating within medical facilities, a charge the militant group has denied.
The overnight attack was not the first time that Nasser Hospital itself has been targeted.
In August 2025, the hospital was hit by a double tap Israeli strik e that killed at least 20 people, including journalists and health workers. The deadly attack sparked international outrage.
Of Gaza’s 37 hospitals, just two are considered to be “fully functioning,” while 18 are partially functioning and 17 are considered nonfunctioning after much of the enclave’s healthcare system was devastated under Israel’s offensive, according to data published by the World Health Organization.
Israeli strikes have continued in Gaza despite a ceasefire agreement reached in October of last year.
More than 1,600 people have been killed since the truce came into effect, according to the Palestinian Health Ministry in the enclave. Israel says four of its ⁠soldiers have ​been killed in that time.
Both Israel and Hamas have accused each other of violating the ceasefire.

articles.title_zh: Israel hits Gaza hospital and France turns away a settler leader, and other Mideast news
articles.content_orig:
An Israeli strike on a hospital in southern Gaza overnight Wednesday killed at least six people, including a doctor and a child, Palestinian officials say.
The strike on Nasser Hospital shortly after midnight hit the complex’s surgery unit, according to a Gaza Civil Defense spokesman. The attack tore through part of the hospital, Ezz Eddine Abu Sabha said, leaving charred debris scattered across the destroyed unit.
The strike killed 52-year-old Dr. Rizk Abu Shaira, Abu Sabha said, as well as a 13-year-old boy who was supposed to have surgery. A total of 40 people were injured in the Israeli strike, including two doctors who are in critical condition.
“People of the world … where can the people of Gaza go? Tents flood, cliffs collapse onto children, and hospitals are bombed with people inside. There is no time for blankets – or tears – to dry,” Dr. Munir Al-Bursh, director-general of Gaza’s Health Ministry, wrote on Facebook.
“Gaza does not ask the world to count its dead … It demands protection for those still alive,” he added.
Footage from inside the hospital showed two bombs, one of which failed to explode. A label on the bomb identified it as a US-manufactured GBU-39/B, a 250-pound bomb that has been supplied to Israel.
“I was asleep when suddenly I was covered with dust and glass,” said Atiya Abu Basir, an elderly patient at the hospital. “I couldn’t walk because I just had surgery.”
Despite a nominal US-brokered ceasefire agreed more than a year ago, Israel has carried out near-daily strikes in Gaza. According to the United Nations, Israeli forces have killed more than 1,400 people in Gaza since the ceasefire, and there is no fully functioning hospital in the devastated enclave.
“They say there is a ceasefire. Where is there a ceasefire? Since the ceasefire, there are more massacres,” said Maryam Abu Hatab, whose brother was killed in the strike. “There are massacres every day in markets, in universities, in the streets. The donkey carts stood by us more than the world’s countries.”
In a statement, the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) said they targeted the commander of Hamas’ Khan Younis Brigade, Muhammad Abu Ismail, as well as “additional terrorists who were hiding inside the Nasser Hospital in Khan Younis.” The IDF said he planned and advanced attacks on Israeli forces and civilians.
CNN reached out to the IDF to ask if Abu Ismail had been killed in the strike and what measures were taken to reduce the risk to civilians.
The US-led Board of Peace, which is tasked with overseeing the ceasefire in Gaza, on Thursday called on Israel and Hamas to uphold their commitments under the Comprehensive Peace Plan and protect civilians after the strike on Nasser Hospital. It also called on all parties to “cede the necessary authority and operational space” to the board to carry out its plan for providing medical care in secure, demilitarized facilities.
Earlier this week, the the board also chided Israel for what it called an “insufficient” response to Gaza flooding . Seasonal rains swamped tens of thousands of tents across the coastal enclave, where nearly two million Palestinians are displaced, according to the United Nations.
“The urgent entry and distribution of essential shelter, sanitation, drainage, and other winterization supplies is critical to protecting civilians,” the board said in a statement Monday, calling on Israel to allow more temporary shelters, waste management, and other supplies.
Israel said that more than 91,000 tents had entered Gaza ahead of winter, but refused to allow in the heavy equipment needed for large-scale cleanup and rubble removal efforts.
“The reconstruction of Gaza can only begin after Hamas fully disarms,” said Israel’s Coordinator for Government Activities in the Territories.
CNN’s Ibrahim Dahman contributed to this article.

articles.title_orig: Colette Kress named Nvidia interim CEO as Jensen Huang's abrupt resignation raises investor concerns
articles.title_zh: Colette Kress named Nvidia interim CEO as Jensen Huang's abrupt resignation raises investor concerns
articles.content_orig:
Fox News contributor Michael Pillsbury discusses the resignation of Nividia CEO Jensen Huang and the long-term controversy with U.S. policy in China.
The abrupt resignation of Jensen Huang as CEO of Nvidia Thursday following reports he engaged in multiple extramarital affairs leaves the AI giant facing an uncertain future, and a longtime company executive is stepping in as interim CEO.
Huang co-founded Nvidia in 1993 and served as its CEO until his resignation, transforming the company from a struggling startup into one of the world's largest by market capitalization amid surging demand for its AI chips. He became a visionary and figurehead for the AI revolution.
Nvidia Chief Financial Officer and EVP Colette Kress has been named the company's interim CEO after serving as Nvidia's CFO since September 2013.
NVIDIA LOSES ITS 'GODFATHER OF AI' AND NOW FACES FIRST BIG TEST WITHOUT HIM
She has deep experience in tech finance, previously working as a CFO for Cisco's business technology and operations finance unit and was also CFO of Microsoft's server and tools division during a 13-year tenure at the software giant.
Analysts view Kress, who has featured prominently in Nvidia's quarterly earnings calls, as a steady hand who can help the company navigate a tumultuous period after the departure of its longtime leader.
Nvidia named chief financial officer Colette Kress as the company's interim CEO following Huang's resignation. (Nvidia/Handout / Reuters)
Bret Kenwell, U.S. investment analyst at eToro, said that while "Huang was more than a CEO and part of the investment thesis ," the selection of longtime Nvidia executive Kress as interim CEO should "provide stability and reassurance" to investors.
"Kress has been a familiar presence at Nvidia and on its conference calls, offering a recognizable voice during an already fragile situation," Kenwell added.
Nvidia is scheduled to report quarterly earnings Tuesday, Nov. 17, which will give Kress an early opportunity to assuage investors' concerns.
Dan Ives, partner and senior managing director at Yorkville Ives, said in a note that "Kress has built enormous credibility internally and externally, and we are big fans of her strategically."
"We always believed she would eventually be CEO of a major public tech company, but she would have to leave Nvidia after many years there," Ives added.
TRUMP SAYS 'THERE IS ONLY ONE MAN' TO REPLACE JENSEN HUANG AS NVIDIA CEO
Nvidia became the preeminent company in the AI space under Huang's leadership and is one of the largest companies in the world by market cap. (Patrick T. Fallon/AFP via Getty Images)
Huang's departure will pose other challenges for Nvidia and Kress given the level of visibility he brought to Nvidia's AI business and his ability to broker deals around the world.
Susannah Streeter, chief investment strategist at Wealth Club, said Kress will be viewed as a "safe pair of hands" who has "been brought into steady leadership, but she lacks global status."
Streeter added that Kress is "unlikely to be able to forge such deep commercial ties, and Nvidia will now enter this period of uncertainty over strategic priorities, pricing and supply agreements."
NVIDIA'S JENSEN HUANG REGIME CHANGE A WARNING TO COMPANIES AND INVESTORS EVERYWHERE, BUSINESS EXPERT CAUTIONS
Jensen Huang served as Nvidia CEO from the time he co-founded the company in 1993 until his resignation on Nov. 12, 2026. (Reuters/Kylie Cooper)
Michael Landsberg, chief investment officer at Landsberg Bennett Private Wealth Management, said Huang's resignation "is the worst-case scenario during this entire saga."
"He was not just a leader, but a visionary for the company, and while CFO Colette Kress is highly capable and respected, there are still big questions about how the innovation of Nvidia will evolve without Jensen."
Gil Luria, managing director at DA Davidson, said "Kress is well respected by investors and should be able to guide Nvidia through this challenging period."

However, Luria cautioned that the "task is daunting, as Nvidia has been founder-led since inception and Mr. Huang concentrated much of the decision-making."
Reuters contributed to this report.

articles.title_orig: Bonds Take Another Beating As Inflation Fears Rise
articles.title_zh: Bonds Take Another Beating As Inflation Fears Rise
articles.content_orig:
U.S. Treasury yields jumped on Thursday, with the 10-year note yield surging above 5%, alongside a move higher in oil prices and expectations of further Federal Reserve hikes.
The yield on the 10-year U.S. Treasury note — the benchmark for mortgages, auto loans and credit card debt — rose more than 13 basis points to 5.125%.
The 2-year Treasury note yield, more sensitive to short-term Fed interest rate decisions, jumped more than 15 basis points to 4.879%. The longer-dated 30-year Treasury bond yield rose 10 basis points to 5.449%.
One basis point equals 0.01%, or 1/100th of 1%, and yields and prices move inversely to one another.
The rise in oil prices came after President Donald Trump said, " We don't need a deal with Iran ," raising concern that the war in the Middle East will continue indefinitely. West Texas Intermediate futures gained more than 2% to close at $88.74 per barrel, while Brent crude was ahead more than 3% to $95.82 per barrel.
Tuesday's hotter-than-expected consumer price index reading has investors anticipating more rate increases from the Fed. Goldman Sachs added another rate hike to its forecast on Wednesday, now expecting an additional quarter percentage point increase in March.
Traders are pricing in 100% odds of an increase in December, with the chance of a half percentage point increase standing at about 13%, according to the CME Group's FedWatch tool.
Another inflation report is due Friday, when the October producer price index, which tracks wholesale prices, is expected to show a 0.4% rise in October, down from the 1.3% surge in September.
On Thursday, investors looked to October's home sales report from the National Association of Realtors, which showed that existing home sales reached their lowest level in more than 16 years last month .
"Fed officials want to push rates even higher to fight inflation, but all this is doing is pushing the housing correction down into the depths of depression," said Chris Rupkey, FWDBONDS chief economist. "It's dark out there with no homebuyers anywhere to be found."
