articles.title_orig: THC drink companies rush to sell inventory as Illinois ban takes effect
articles.title_zh: THC drink companies rush to sell inventory as Illinois ban takes effect
articles.content_orig:
Why are we asking for donations?
A display of THC beverages at the Humboldt Park offices of Perfectly Dosed. The company makes THC emulsion ingredients for a number of companies, including about 50 Illinois businesses.
Provided by South Loop Market
Marz Community Brewing Co. recovered from the post-pandemic downturn with the help of hemp-derived THC beverages.
Their infused line, which includes low-dose and high-potency THC seltzers with playful names like Bong Water and High Tea, has grown to account for nearly half the company’s production at its headquarters in McKinley Park and its Logan Square nanobrewery and taproom.
“It truly rescued our business and allowed us to expand,” Marz founder Ed Marszewski said.
Ed Marszewski, owner of Marz Brewing, stands in front of a fridge of a collection of non-alcoholic drinks at Life on Marz at 1950 N. Western, Wednesday, Nov. 26, 2025. | Anthony Vazquez/Sun-Times
Strong local demand for THC drinks even pushed the company to relocate some of its beer production to Louisville, Kentucky, where its partner Against the Grain Brewery has co-packed and brewed several Marz beers the last few years.
But with the state’s looming Nov. 12 deadline banning nearly every intoxicating hemp product on the market, Marszewski and many other Chicago businesses must make some tough decisions.
“We’re going to have to lay people off,” Marszewski said. “We won’t have enough income to pay them.”
The ban is part a wide-ranging bill, signed by Gov. JB Pritzker in June , that overhauls cannabis and hemp regulations. But the Illinois Healthy Alternatives Association and a group of hemp businesses filed an emergency motion on Friday for a temporary restraining order saying the law is unconstitutional and would “obliterate the businesses of thousands of Illinois farmers, infusers, distributors, and retailers.”
The state’s timetable mimicked federal guidelines set in President Donald Trump’s 2025 spending bill that also outlawed hemp potency limits beyond 0.4 milligrams of THC per container. Previously, hemp-based THC products were federally defined as having less than 0.3% THC, the active ingredient in cannabis.
In September, the federal deadline was extended to Dec. 11, but Illinois has stuck with the original November deadline — keeping the pressure on beverage manufacturers, retailers, restaurants, grocery stores, entertainment venues and other stakeholders.
With Illinois businesses required to exit the category a month ahead of other states, local breweries are at a particular disadvantage against neighboring competitors, according to Jonathan Fritz, partner at Hopewell Brewing Co., which launched its popular lemon-lime-flavored THC drink Choom in 2024 before expanding to sparkling waters and teas.
Hopewell Brewing Co. launched its popular lemon-lime-flavored THC drink Choom in 2024 but will be winding down the product following new regulations for hemp-based THC products.
As part of an inventory wind down, the company is offering 50% off Choom products at its Logan Square headquarters, where it also co-manufactures THC beverages for other brands.
“Our state legislators have missed the mark here, and this decision directly damages local craft businesses like ours,” Fritz said.
Hopewell’s THC line has been carried at Parson’s Chicken & Fish, Foxtrot and other stores, accounting for nearly a third of its on-premises sales, the company told the Sun-Times last year.
Revolution Brewing, Chicago’s largest independent craft brewer, halted production of its Reverb THC beverage line in the summer.
Revolution owner Josh Deth hopes Congress can find a resolution and that Illinois lawmakers follow suit by allowing distribution through licensed liquor establishments, a carve-out strongly favored by alcohol suppliers, distributors and retailers.
“There’s clear customer demand for low-dosage THC beverages for both drinking at home and going out, and we’d love to keep innovating within the THC drink space if we are allowed too,” he said.
London-based research firm Euromonitor International estimated the hemp-based THC beverage market will skyrocket to $4.1 billion by 2028, an eye-popping 1,615% increase from $239 million in 2023.
Humboldt Park-based Perfectly Dosed makes THC emulsion ingredients for about 50 Illinois beverage brands, breweries and restaurants. It’s planning to move some warehousing and fulfillment services out of state if restrictions are prolonged.
Several of its partners and suppliers extract hemp in Colorado, which has emerged as a potential build-out site due its safe harbor laws.
“We do have to consider that as an option,” Perfectly Dosed co-founder Glenn McElfresh said. “The question that a lot of businesses are facing, including ourselves right now, is where do we invest that future CapEx [capital expenditure] for our business?”
Perfectly Dosed Vice President of Government Affairs Glenn McElfresh, CEO Alexander Choi and Vice President of Business Development Liam Rigney at the company’s headquarters in Humboldt Park. The co-founders plan to move some warehousing and fulfillment services out of state if Illinois’ hemp restrictions are enacted and prolonged.
Barry Brecheisen/For the Sun-Times
His assessment of the Illinois market has changed drastically since about a year ago when he told the Sun-Times that Chicago could become the heart of the hemp beverage industry.
“Because of the law, we can’t definitely say we’re going to build in Illinois,” McElfresh said.
Perfectly Dosed plans to apply for a newly established hemp product manufacturing license administered through the Illinois Department of Agriculture.
Licenses will be required for any business or person handling, processing and extracting hemp in Illinois, as well as manufacturing any product with hemp-extracted cannabinoids or any hemp-derived product, according to the Illinois Department of Agriculture.
Manufacturing licenses will be issued after applications and on-site inspections are completed and a $5,000 fee is paid.
The department didn’t share how many businesses have already applied for a license but said in a statement that it’s working with “several applicants as they complete the process.” It also said that it’s “accepting applications for both hemp manufacturing and industrial hemp processor licenses on a rolling basis, with no application deadline.”
Cresco Labs CEO Charlie Bachtell said it supports regulatory standards for all THC products. The Chicago-based vertically integrated company operates 10 stores in Illinois, including two in Chicago.
“Consumers deserve to know what they’re buying and that they can rely on production and testing standards for products they ingest,” he said.
A sign warning of an impending ban on some THC beverages stands outside of a BP gas station at 1221 S. Wabash Ave. on Tuesday, Oct. 27, 2026.
Tim O’Hern, chief operating officer of Nature’s Grace and Wellness in Fulton County, expects several products sold outside licensed cannabis channels to transition into the regulated market.
“THC beverages represent one of the fastest growing product categories in the regulated cannabis industry,” O’Hern said. Nature’s Grace operates nine stores in Illinois, including three in Chicago.
Cannabis product sales in Ohio’s regulated market increased significantly since the state implemented a hemp products ban in March, benefiting companies like Chicago-based Verano Holdings, which operates six stores in the state.
“According to state data, total receipts were up 25% at the end of the third quarter versus the end of the first quarter, a notable positive trend that correlates with the start of the hemp ban, which indicates hemp consumers are shifting towards licensed dispensaries,” Verano Holdings founder and CEO George Archos told analysts last month.
Under Illinois’ new guidelines, hemp-derived THC products over the federal potency threshold must be sold only at state-licensed cannabis dispensaries and be taxed the same as cannabis products

articles.title_orig: Putin takes hard line in US talks as Ukraine says Starlink disrupted again
articles.title_zh: Putin takes hard line in US talks as Ukraine says Starlink disrupted again
articles.content_orig:
Russian president says he would target any foreign troops sent to Ukraine and refuses to soften territorial demands
Vladimir Putin warned US negotiators that Russia would target any foreign troops deployed to Ukraine, in a series of hardline remarks that came as the Ukrainian military faced renewed disruptions to Elon Musk’s Starlink satellite service.
During the talks at the Kremlin with the US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff on Thursday, the Russian president refused to soften his territorial demands, insisting on full control over four Ukrainian regions that Moscow claims to have annexed.
He also ruled out accepting the deployment of foreign peacekeeping troops in Ukraine , describing such a move as a “continuation of war”.
Putin’s comments appeared to severely dampen hopes that a peace deal could be within reach, after Volodymyr Zelenskyy said there was a “window of opportunity” to reach an agreement before the end of 2026.
The latest trip to Moscow by Witkoff and Kushner, who have made numerous visits to Russia, was partly aimed at securing European participation in future negotiations, according to two people familiar with the talks.
Speaking after the meeting, Witkoff confirmed that European representatives would join the next round of talks. “They’re our partners, and it’s important for them to be involved,” he told reporters as he boarded a plane leaving Moscow.
The US envoys will now travel to Dublin, Ireland, where they will meet Zelenskyy and debrief him on the Moscow meeting.
Andy Burnham, the British prime minister, said national security adviser Jonathan Powell would join the talks in Berlin.
Amid a flurry of diplomatic activity, including the recent talks in Abu Dhabi, the Kremlin appears to have succeeded in reframing negotiations over the war in Ukraine as part of a broader discussion about European security.
But Europe is wary of Russian attempts to focus discussions on a European security architecture, while Moscow continues to pound Ukraine with bombs and missiles.
The EU foreign policy chief, Kaja Kallas, told reporters: “We already have a European security architecture in place.” Kallas pointed to the cold war-era Helsinki accords and the Budapest memorandum , which guaranteed the territorial integrity of Ukraine. “The problem is that Russia is not keeping to those agreements, so right now the focus should be that Russia actually keeps to their obligations … and they don’t attack another country again.” Focusing on a European security architecture was a “distraction” without a ceasefire, she added.
Both Washington and Moscow have been urging European leaders to appoint a single representative to lead negotiations on their behalf.
“Once a representative is appointed, a chief negotiator authorised to speak on Europe’s behalf, there will be a four-way dialogue,” Putin said on Thursday.
EU leaders are due to discuss the issue of who speaks for Europe on Friday, but so far have declined to nominate one person to speak for the bloc. One EU official said the EU would be represented by its institutions when issues concerning the union were on the table, but played down any imminent appointment. They said: “Do I expect an agreement on a special representative? My answer is no, I don’t.”
Kallas suggested she – as the EU’s high representative for foreign and security policy – should represent the EU in talks, alongside António Costa, the president of the European Council.
More than 45 European leaders are meeting in Dublin for the European Political Community summit, a gathering that brings together nearly every country on the continent, apart from the leaders of Belarus and Russia.
The French president, Emmanuel Macron, played down the importance of having a single European negotiator, saying “the content determines the format”. “There is no more US support. So there [are] some mediations, fine,” he said, referring to the process led by Kushner and Witkoff. “But at the end of the day we will be the one to define and decide for our future security as Europeans.”
The German chancellor, Friedrich Merz, said it was first necessary to get Putin to the negotiating table before deciding on a European envoy. Merz said: “It’s not about individuals. What matters is that Putin is prepared to hold talks.”
Meanwhile, Zelenskyy accused Musk’s Starlink satellite service of damaging Ukraine’s ability to defend itself against Russian drone attacks, after Ukrainian military officials reported new restrictions on the system.
According to Zelenskyy, Starshield, a military version of Starlink funded by the Pentagon, has for several days been subject to speed limits of 100mph (161km/h) along the frontline and in Russian-occupied territory.
Similar restrictions last month prompted confusion over who had ordered them, with Musk and the Trump administration pointing fingers at each other before the service was partly restored.
The latest restrictions had made it harder for Ukrainian forces to intercept Russia’s increasingly sophisticated jet-powered drones, Zelenskyy said, accusing the service of “helping the Russians kill more Ukrainians and carry out more accurate strikes against Ukraine”.
Kyiv has contacted Washington to seek an explanation for the disruption, which Zelenskyy said appeared to be deliberate rather than a technical fault.

articles.title_orig: Moment Greta Thunberg laughs at climate protests she started after ditching cause for Gaza: ‘They’re still doing that?’
articles.title_zh: Moment Greta Thunberg laughs at climate protests she started after ditching cause for Gaza: ‘They’re still doing that?’
articles.content_orig:
By ELIANA SILVER, SENIOR FOREIGN NEWS REPORTER
Published: 09:28 EST, 12 November 2026 | Updated: 12:55 EST, 12 November 2026
Greta Thunberg has featured in a documentary appearing to mock protesters still participting in the climate movement she started.
Fridays for Future was launched by Thunberg in 2018, when she was just 15, after she began skipping school on Fridays to demand action on climate change .
What began in Sweden quickly snowballed into a global movement, inspiring millions of students to walk out of classrooms and take to the streets in rallies around the world.
But in a newly released documentary titled 'On Tanks into the Climate Crisis – How Activism is Criminalised', the now 23-year-old appeared shocked when told that a Fridays for Future demonstration was taking place in Berlin .
'Is it?' she asked, looking visibly surprised, before bursting into loud laughter. 'Really? They still do that?' she shrieked.
An activist friend sitting beside her joined in the laughter, before Thunberg turned towards the camera and shouted: 'Cut!'
Thunberg first rose to fame as the face of the youth climate movement. In recent years, however, her activism has increasingly shifted towards vocal support for the pro-Palestinian cause.
'Really? They still do that?' Thunberg shrieked, while laughing loudly
An activist friend sitting beside her joined in the laughter, before Thunberg turned towards the camera and shouted: 'Cut!'
Thunberg first rose to fame as the face of the youth climate movement
Last winter, she was arrested in central London at a protest supporting jailed Palestine Action protesters on hunger strike.
Footage showed the 22-year-old activist holding a sign saying 'I support Palestine Action prisoners, I oppose genocide' outside the headquarters of an insurance firm.
A City of London Police officer can be seen taking away the placard before asking Thunberg to stand.
Around the same time, Thunberg spoke out in support of several imprisoned Palestine Action activists who were on hunger strike.
She described them as 'political prisoners' and joined calls for the charges against them to be dropped.
She was also detained last year by Israel after warships intercepted the aid flotilla headed for Gaza she was on.
Thunberg's detention was the second such incident, after she was also taken by Israeli forces while onboard a separate ship headed for the Palestinian state last June.
Most recently, she spoke in support of rapper Macklemore after he was dropped from Ed Sheeran's tour for pro-Palestine statements made at one of his concerts.
The 23-year-old publicly backed Sheeran's 'cancellation', criticising him in a statement shared online.
In a statement on Instagram, Thunberg said: 'We are witnessing one of the biggest artists in the world being cancelled because they tried to 'both sides' Israel's genocide against the Palestinian people.
'This is a clear and undeniable sign that the global consciousness has shifted. The normalisation of an apartheid state, and the attempts to sanitise or justify its actions, will no longer be tolerated. Ed, there is only one victim here: the Palestinian people.'
Following her recent comments appearing to mock climate protesters, the Swede has faced strong backlash online.
One person on X commented: 'Climate was just the warm-up. Hating Israel is the real job.'
Another person added: 'It suddenly isn't a problem anymore. So much for climate 'emergency'. Just shows the credibility that she has.'
'Fridays for Future was a cult-like movement from the start, whose leaders secretly mocked the protesters back then and now openly mock them on camera,' said a third.
Others have come to her defense, arguing she was simply mocking the protests for not being 'radical' enough.
'The point is that she finds the FFF protest too nice, too conformist and too middle-class. She laughs at its lack of radicalism. If she is now accused of not caring about climate protection, that is wrong and an oversimplification. What matters to her is the form of protest itself,' an X user commented under the video.
Thunberg arrived at UN climate talks on Tuesday, in her first appearance since the 2021 talks in Glasgow, where she went viral for dismissing world leaders' promises as 'blah, blah, blah.'
Thunberg, who was part of the Global Sumud Flotilla, arriving in Athens
In December, Thunberg was arrested in central London at a protest supporting jailed Palestine Action protesters
Thunberg arrived at UN climate talks on Tuesday, in her first appearance since the 2021 talks in Glasgow
The COP31 conference is being held in the Turkish resort city of Antalya following a year of deadly climate-related disasters, including heat waves and floods, and another energy shock caused by the Iran war.
'It's a hypocrisy every year that the host countries are given an opportunity to whitewash themselves and we know that these negotiations are filled with lobbyists, paid by the very destructive industries which are benefiting from our extremely violent status quo,' Thunberg said as she arrived.
'Our political and economic systems that have become incompatible with human nature.'
COP31 co-hosts Turkey and Australia are promoting renewable energy and rooftop solar installations, but both still rely heavily on fossil fuels, especially coal, to generate electricity.
Previous hosts, including Brazil, the United Arab Emirates and Azerbaijan, are major oil producers.
Climate change is 'threatening everything,' Thunberg said, warning that 'everything and everyone we love is at stake.'
'We should act to protect and benefit people rather than constantly sacrificing the global majority and the very planet we are all living on, for a fortunate few to keep making unimaginable profits and maintaining geopolitical power,' she added.

articles.title_orig: US home sales fall to lowest level since 2010 as mortgage rates soar
articles.title_zh: US home sales fall to lowest level since 2010 as mortgage rates soar
articles.content_orig:
Home sales fell to their lowest since 2010, a new report shows, in large part due to high mortgage rates. Mario Tama/Getty Images hide caption
The housing market has finally broken out of the stagnant holding pattern it's been stuck in for more than four years – just not in the right direction.
Existing home sales in October fell to 3.75 million, making an 8.8% decline in sales from a year earlier, according to the National Association of Realtors. The last time sales were this low was 16 years ago.
"It was a punch in the gut," said Joel Berner, senior economist at Realtor.com . "We expected to see a soft month but not the softest month since 2010."
The drop is mainly due to high mortgage rates.
In October, the average rate for a 30-year fixed rate mortgage hit as high as 7.40%, the highest since 2023. Rates have gone down a bit since then, but are still well above where they were a year ago.
Higher inflation and bond yields have driven up mortgage rates, but some of this housing slowdown was by design.
The Federal Reserve raised its benchmark interest rate in September to increase the cost of borrowing, including home mortgages. Fewer home sales and other purchases mean less economic activity, which the Fed wants in order to reach its goal of lowering inflation.
Policymakers at the Fed have signaled another rate hike could come in December, which could further slow down the housing market.
"It might seem like kicking the housing market while it's down right now for the Fed to continue a rate raising cycle but in the long run getting inflation under control is really the goal," Berner said.

articles.title_orig: Google announces Gemini 4 Hydrogen with ‘significant leaps’ in speed, intelligence
articles.title_zh: Google announces Gemini 4 Hydrogen with ‘significant leaps’ in speed, intelligence
articles.content_orig:
After this week’s Carbon availability , Google today unveiled Gemini 4 Hydrogen instead of keeping the “Flash” branding. This model is billed as bringing “cutting-edge intelligence to everyone.”
Compared to Gemini 3.8 Flash (which launched in September), Hydrogen is billed as a “major standalone upgrade” with “significant leaps in both speed and intelligence.” It offers native 1 million-token input and up to 1 million output tokens. Specifically:
“Hydrogen surpasses Argon on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at its default high thinking level (51 vs. 50, and reaching 54 at its highest xhigh thinking setting), while often completing tasks faster than models in its class.”
In the Gemini app, Hydrogen is better at following and sticking to your tone, format, and rules, while offering clear tables and visual breakdowns. As such, “email drafts, study guides, rewrites, and documents come back ready to use on the first try.” Additionally, Hydrogen “more frequently calls the right tools (i.e., Connected Apps) and skills for the job.”
In the model picker, 4 Hydrogen is billed as providing “Everyday help.”
Free users in the Gemini app get access to Hydrogen via the “[Auto] model selection when it’s the appropriate model for the prompt.”
Google says Hydrogen significantly upgrades Search (AI Mode) by better understanding your intent:
…you can ask your question in your natural flow of thought — even if you have multiple parts to your query, hard-to-understand typos, or highly specific requests — and Search will intelligently comprehend what you’re looking for.
Responses get more visual and will feature a wider range of relevant links. Hydrogen is the default model for AI Mode and is used for “your hardest questions” in AI Overviews.
This naming scheme is not the most intuitive.
In Google Antigravity, 4 Hydrogen has an “Extra” thinking tier alongside Low, Medium, and High. Then there’s Orchestrator: “Carbon that may offload routine steps to Hydrogen. Same Carbon-level quality, fewer tokens used.”
To help make this multi-model collaboration automatic, we’re introducing Orchestrator in Google Antigravity . Rather than using a single model from start to finish, Orchestrator dynamically switches between models like Carbon and Hydrogen within the same session.
For workflows that require parallel agents, Carbon can act as the coordinator while Hydrogen can power worker and verifier agents to build and test changes simultaneously across isolated workspaces — helping teams ship complex projects faster without driving up token costs.
Hydrogen is available in Antigravity for paid Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers.
For developers, Hydrogen costs $1.50 per million input tokens and $7.50 per million output tokens.

articles.title_zh: Nasdaq wavers as traders weigh Nvidia CEO exit, AMD climbs: Live updates
articles.content_orig:
The Nasdaq Composite fluctuated on Thursday as investors assessed the departure of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang , betting it would not derail the whole AI trade.
The tech-heavy Nasdaq was last down 0.3%, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average traded around the flatline. The S&P 500 fell 0.1%.
Selling pressure on Nvidia eased a bit, with the stock last down 5%. The shares were down double digits at one point after the company announced that Huang had resigned and named CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO. This comes after Huang reportedly had an affair with an alleged Chinese spy.
Investors moved into competitors of Nvidia, including Advanced Micro Devices and Broadcom , helping to bolster the market. AMD shares were up 4%, while Broadcom gained 5%.
Hyperscalers Microsoft and Alphabet — key buyers of Nvidia chips and leaders of the AI rally — also increased.
"This is a golden opportunity for Amazon, for Google, for AMD, for Broadcom, for OpenAI and Anthropic, who are hiring chip experts to help them design their own chips," said Jed Ellerbroek, portfolio manager at Argent Capital Management.
"Nvidia's fate as one company is one thing, but this AI revolution is way bigger than that," he also said. "If Nvidia falls from grace and their chips are no longer the best, and AMDs are better or Google's are better, then people will switch over and buy them. The demand for the chips is not is not going down."
There was a sense from investors that perhaps Huang's exit was a capitulation event for the AI trade with Nvidia's stock down by more than 25% the past one month as this scandal was unfolding.
"We are sticking with the thesis that technology stocks bottomed last week," said Tom Lee, the head of research at Fundstrat, in a note Thursday. Huang's departure "does not change our view."
Stocks outside of technology such as JPMorgan and Eli Lilly traded higher as well.
Stephanie Link said Thursday she sold her Nvidia following Jensen Huang's resignation from his post as CEO, with the investor moving into another artificial intelligence play: Micron Technology .
"The fundamentals are very, very strong at [Nvidia], and I expect the quarter next week to be very good with 300 billion in free cash flow next year," Link, the chief investment strategist at Hightower Advisors, said on CNBC's " Halftime Report ." "But, this stock is not going to trade on fundamentals ... for a while because you have the overhang of the investigations of leadership changes of potential departures."

Nvidia shares were trading down 4% on Thursday after Jensen Huang announced he would immediately step down as CEO and a member of the board at the chipmaker.
The stock hovered just under $4 trillion in market cap, after paring steeper losses earlier in the day of more than 10%. Nvidia has closed above the market cap benchmark since July 2025.
Read the full story here .
Paul Meeks says he's buying Nvidia shares with "both hands" despite CEO Jensen Huang's resignation , because the decline amid this unfolding scandal has brought the stock down to "stupid" valuation levels.
The Freedom Capital head of technology research noted that the stock is trading at just 10 times fiscal 2028 earnings estimates after Thursday's decline.
Nvidia shares are off 20% in November alone, pressured by the scandal unfolding.
"I think that the actual announcement of his resignation is a market-clearing event," said Meeks.
CNBC Pro subscribers can learn more about Meeks' other key points here .
Even as Nvidia shares remained lower following CEO Jensen Huang's resignation , the broader market rose as investors moved past the announcement.
The S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite , both of which began Thursday's session lower, rose 0.2% and 0.1%, respectively.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average outperformed, rising 138 points, or 0.3%.
Sales of existing homes fell to their lowest level in more than 16 years during October, the National Association of Realtors reported Thursday.
A decline of 5.5% brought the seasonally adjusted annualized rate down to 3.75 million during a month that saw mortgage rates continue to climb, putting pressure on an already beleaguered housing market. The total was the lowest since August 2010.
"Home buying is difficult when mortgage rates have climbed to their highest levels since 2000, aside from a single month in 2023," said NAR chief economist Lawrence Yun. "Based on the current underwhelming home sales pace at a time of consistent job growth, there could be sizable pent-up demand if mortgage rates decline."
Nvidia shares are seeing huge volume as the stock drops following the resignation of CEO Jensen Huang .
The chipmaker saw more than 373 million shares traded amid the selling pressure. That's above the stock's 30-day average of 144.4 million.
The stock was last down more than 5%.
Cleveland Federal Reserve President Beth Hammack said Thursday she doesn't see the need for aggressive interest rate increases ahead.
While Hammack still supports rate hikes as the Fed struggles to get inflation back to its 2% target, she advocated for a gradual approach that the economy can adapt to more easily.
"I think we need to move rates higher to get to a restrictive stance of policy to bring inflation back down to 2%. My view is that if we go steadily in smaller increments, more frequent, smaller rises, it's easier for businesses and households to manage around that," she sad. "It's less disruptive to the overall economy than moving in sharper, more aggressive movements."
Earlier in the week, Fed Governor Christopher Waller raised the specter of a half-point hike at the December meeting if the inflation data comes in worse than anticipated. However, Hammack said she doesn't think that's necessary, at least for now.
"If we get behind the curve, and I don't think we're behind the curve today, but if we get behind the curve, then that might be something that we need to consider," she said. "So I'll certainly have an open mind walking into that December meeting."
The S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite began Thursday's session in the red.
The broad market index fell 0.8% shortly after the opening bell, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq declined 1.5%. The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 108 points, or 0.2%.
Shares of Broadcom and Advanced Micro Devices gained about 3% each in premarket trading after Jensen Huang resigned as CEO of Nvidia.
The company's chief financial officer Colette Kress has been named interim chief.
Nvidia shares were last down about 10%.

The stock was last down almost 16%. That's after it rose more than 15% in Wednesday's regular session.

articles.title_orig: Here's what Nvidia interim CEO Colette Kress and board chair Harvey Jones wrote to Nvidia employees
articles.title_zh: Here's what Nvidia interim CEO Colette Kress and board chair Harvey Jones wrote to Nvidia employees
articles.content_orig:
On the heels of founder Jensen Huang's resignation as CEO of Nvidia , new interim CEO Colette Kress and board chair Harvey Jones sent emails to employees Thursday expressing gratitude and optimism for the future.
CNBC obtained copies of the emails from a source familiar with the matter, who said Jones sent the first email and Kress replied shortly after.
Follow CNBC's live coverage of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's resignation
"The Board, Estaff and I recognize that this has been an extraordinarily difficult period and I want you to know how grateful we are for your resilience, professionalism and continued dedication," Kress wrote in her email.
The term Estaff is commonly used to refer to executive staff, the group of direct reports to C-suite executives at a company. Nvidia will host a company meeting on November 18 at 9am PST, her email said.
Board chair Jones took a similar tone in his email, and praised Kress as "a key architect of NVIDIA's growth and capital strategy."
"The Board has full confidence in Colette to deliver on our commitments to shareholders, customers, partners, and to each of you," Jones wrote.
Below are the staff emails obtained by CNBC on Thursday.
I believe deeply in this company and in its future. More than anything, I believe in each of you, in our customers and partners and in the vital role we play every day in the global economy.
The Board, Estaff and I recognize that this has been an extraordinarily difficult period and I want you to know how grateful we are for your resilience, professionalism and continued dedication. Thank you.
This company has achieved so much because of the work that all of you bring to it every single day. You are our greatest strength. You will hear more from leadership in the coming days about our future together, and we will host a company meeting on November 18 at 9am PT.
We play a vital role in building the technology that is powering the AI revolution, and we have important work ahead of us. So let's move forward together, with the same determination and commitment that have always defined this company.
Thank you for all you do, Colette
I am writing to share an important update. Jensen has resigned as CEO and Board Member, and the Board has asked our Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress to serve as interim CEO while it conducts a search for a permanent successor looking at both internal and external candidates. I will serve as the first-ever Chair of the Board.
As CFO for over 13 years, Colette has been a key architect of NVIDIA's growth and capital strategy. She possesses a deep understanding of this business and the markets in which we operate. The Board has full confidence in Colette to deliver on our commitments to shareholders, customers, partners, and to each of you.
Jensen's contributions to NVIDIA are profound. NVIDIA is one of the most consequential technology companies in the world. We pioneered accelerated computing, defined the modern GPU, and built the platform that powered artificial intelligence.
The Board takes seriously our duty as stewards of this great company.
The strength of this company resides in our employees, leadership team, technical strength and partner ecosystem. I am confident that under Colette's leadership, with the full support of the Board, we will continue to grow our business, and lead the industry forward. Thank you for your focus, your professionalism, and your commitment to NVIDIA.
Harvey Jones Chair, NVIDIA Board of Directors

articles.title_orig: Trump says Apple’s Tim Cook should take over Nvidia
articles.title_zh: Trump says Apple’s Tim Cook should take over Nvidia
articles.content_orig:
Sen. Pete Ricketts, R-Neb., discusses the resignation of Jensen Huang as CEO of Nvidia, the need for an investigations and the national security implications if China gains access to U.S. chips on 'Varney & Co.'
President Donald Trump suggested Thursday that former Apple CEO Tim Cook should replace Jensen Huang as the head of Nvidia following Huang's abrupt resignation amid scrutiny of his personal conduct and potential national security concerns.
"NOW THAT Nvidia CEO JENSEN HUANG, who has done a fantastic job, has resigned, there is only one man to take his place - TIM COOK of Apple. A Legend replaces a Legend!" Trump wrote on Truth Social.
The president's endorsement comes as Nvidia faces a leadership shake-up following Huang's departure from the artificial intelligence chipmaker he co-founded in 1993.
NVIDIA CEO JENSEN HUANG RESIGNS AMID INVESTIGATION INTO RELATIONSHIP WITH ALLEGED CHINESE SPY
Jensen Huang, chief executive officer of Nvidia Corp., and President Donald Trump. (Graeme Sloan/Bonnie Cash/UPI/Bloomberg)
Nvidia named Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress interim CEO on Thursday while its board searches for a permanent successor, considering candidates from both inside and outside the company.
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang speaks during the G20 Innovation Ministerial on Sept. 2, 2026, in Chapel Hill, North Carolina. (Sean Rayford/Getty Images)
Cook stepped down as Apple's CEO in September after 15 years at the helm and now serves as the iPhone maker's executive chairman. Trump did not indicate whether Cook had expressed interest in taking the helm at Nvidia.
Huang's resignation followed reports of two extramarital affairs, including a relationship with a Chinese businesswoman whom U.S. authorities suspect of spying for Beijing.
The allegations raised questions about whether the longtime technology executive could have been targeted by Chinese intelligence, given Nvidia's central role in the global artificial intelligence industry and ongoing U.S.-China tensions over advanced chips.
No evidence has been publicly established that Huang disclosed confidential information or that the woman obtained Nvidia secrets. (Artur Widak/NurPhoto)
The reported relationship has fueled concerns about potential foreign intelligence efforts to gain access to sensitive information involving one of America's most strategically important technology companies. However, no evidence has been publicly established that Huang disclosed confidential information or that the woman obtained Nvidia secrets.

Trump had previously defended Huang, saying Monday that he believed the executive's account that he was unaware of the woman's alleged intelligence ties.

articles.title_orig: The Bank of Nvidia just lost its banker — here’s where the AI trade is exposed
articles.title_zh: The Bank of Nvidia just lost its banker — here’s where the AI trade is exposed
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
Jensen Huang didn't just sell chips for the AI boom. He helped pay for it, and Wall Street is now repricing everyone on his tab.
Huang resigned as Nvidia's ( NVDA ) CEO and left its board Thursday, effective immediately, after reports of two affairs , one involving an alleged Chinese spy. CFO Colette Kress is now interim CEO, and the company still plans to report earnings Tuesday.
Nvidia stock sank to its lowest level in more than a year, putting it briefly $2 trillion below its October record. But the selling hasn't hit the AI trade evenly . Nebius ( NBIS ) and CoreWeave ( CRWV ), cloud companies that rent out Nvidia chips, took the worst of it, while rivals Broadcom ( AVGO ) and AMD ( AMD ) and most of Big Tech held up.
That pattern traces the Bank of Nvidia .
Nvidia owns stakes in Intel ( INTC ), SpaceX ( SPCX ), CoreWeave, Coherent ( COHR ) and Safe Superintelligence, bought $3 billion of Meta's ( META ) stock offering, and has pledged up to $10 billion to Anthropic ahead of its IPO next week . It holds a $30 billion stake in OpenAI and has a preliminary deal to invest as much as $100 billion more. Many of those companies turn around and buy Nvidia's chips.
Nvidia's latest quarterly filing lists about $530 billion in commitments and guarantees, by Yahoo Finance's count, including roughly $65 billion to rent back cloud capacity from companies like CoreWeave and a guarantee of up to $105 billion on OpenAI's Ohio data center leases.
"It does bring into question what we've been talking about for ... the better part of the last year, which is a lot of these circular relationships," Liz Thomas, chief market strategist at SoFi, said at Yahoo Finance Invest .
The first is the dealmaker himself. Huang sat at the center of these deals, and Kress, who signed off on them as CFO, now decides how many more to write.
The OpenAI guarantee pays out only if OpenAI defaults, and the kind of downturn that would sink OpenAI would likely hit Nvidia's own sales at the same time.
Customers are paying slower too. Nvidia's receivables hit $63 billion last quarter, with bills taking about 60 days to collect, up from 45. Nvidia blamed longer terms on big deals.
And its own portfolio is shrinking. The value of Nvidia's largest public stock holdings has lost more than $20 billion in value since June, led by Intel.
The money behind the AI build-out was already getting harder to find. CoreWeave's CEO said this week the company won't borrow without collateral at today's high rates. BofA's Savita Subramanian told Yahoo Finance the tech giants are now selling more of their own stock than they buy back, saying they're "net issuers today rather than buying back their stock."
Nvidia's balance sheet is the counterweight, with about $99 billion in cash and securities against $33 billion of debt at the end of July.
Tuesday's earnings report will show whether Kress stands behind the guidance and the commitments, and whether customers are paying on time.
Thomas put the question for next week bluntly.

articles.title_orig: Singapore Says Warns Alice Huang, Lacks Evidence of Offenses
articles.title_zh: Singapore Says Warns Alice Huang, Lacks Evidence of Offenses
articles.content_orig:
Singapore’s government said on Thursday the United States had provided little help in its investigation into Alice Huang, the woman at the center of a spy plot that has led to the investigation of Nvidia’s chief executive, Jensen Huang .
Singaporean authorities held Ms. Huang’s passport to prevent her from leaving the country from June 2025 until February over “potential false declarations” in relation to her company, Megaspeed, which is based in the country, the government said in a statement. She was ultimately released with a “stern warning” and barred from re-entering Singapore.
The statement raises new questions about the response of the Trump administration to the case and why the U.S. government did not more forcefully intervene. According to the timeline in the statement, Singaporean authorities had been holding Ms. Huang’s passport well after President Trump was briefed last fall about her relationship with Nvidia’s chief executive and the belief that she was a Chinese intelligence asset.
The New York Times has reported that Taiwan began monitoring Ms. Huang in 2024 at the guidance of the U.S. government.
In its statement, Singapore said that it had sought information from an American server maker and close Nvidia business partner, Supermicro, but that the company had provided “limited cooperation.” Supermicro, a firm that packages Nvidia’s A.I. chips onto servers that can be used in data centers, has been at the center of a number of chip smuggling investigations across the globe.
Supermicro was a supplier to Megaspeed, a company incorporated in Singapore and run by Ms. Huang, according to two people with knowledge of the matter.
Singapore said in the statement its authorities raised Supermicro’s “limited cooperation” with the U.S. Department of Justice and Federal Bureau of Investigation in July 2025 and “requested their assistance in securing the company’s cooperation.”
“Despite these repeated requests, Singapore has to date received limited information or assistance in respect of the company,” the statement said.
Supermicro denied that Megaspeed had ever been a customer. “Supermicro did not sell any products to Megaspeed and has operated in compliance with all applicable U.S. export and re-export control laws,” the company said in a statement.
During questioning, Ms. Huang sought to downplay her role in Megaspeed, according to Singapore’s statement. She was ultimately released because of “insufficient evidence relating to the possible inaccurate declarations for which Megaspeed was being investigated.”
She was issued a “stern warning” and barred from re-entering Singapore. The country’s police are continuing to investigate Megaspeed.
Paul Mozur is the global technology correspondent for The Times, based in Taipei. Previously he wrote about technology and politics in Asia from Hong Kong, Shanghai and Seoul.

articles.content_orig:
The Israeli military struck a hospital in the southern Gaza Strip on Thursday, killing at least six people and injuring 28 more, according to local health officials.
Dr. Ahmed al-Farra, general director of Nasser Hospital, said in a news conference on Thursday that two missiles had hit the facility and that among the dead was Rezeq Abu Shaira, 52, a doctor.
Health officials reached in Gaza by phone said that a man called Khaled Abu Anza had also been killed. A spokeswoman for the Israeli military, speaking on condition of anonymity in line with protocol, said that Mr. Abu Anza was a Hamas operative.
The Israeli security agency and military said in a joint statement on Thursday that they had targeted Muhammad Abu Ismail, whom they identified as a Hamas commander “responsible for holding numerous hostages captive” during the Gaza war.
The Israeli authorities said that Hamas had established a command center at the hospital complex to stage operations against Israeli forces and was storing weapons there. They added that steps had been taken to mitigate harm to civilians.
Hamas said the Israeli claim that the hospital was used for military activity was a “blatant attempt to justify a heinous crime targeting a civilian medical facility.” Residents of Gaza have said that officials affiliated with Hamas-run Gaza government and security forces sometimes use the enclave’s hospitals as offices.

articles.title_orig: Senator opens investigation into evidence RFK Jr ‘unlawfully lied’ to Congress
articles.title_zh: Senator opens investigation into evidence RFK Jr ‘unlawfully lied’ to Congress
articles.content_orig:
Exclusive: Ron Wyden, citing Guardian report, is launching inquiry into whether health secretary lied about Samoa trip during confirmation hearings
A top Democratic senator has launched an investigation into evidence that Robert F Kennedy Jr “unlawfully lied” in his 2025 confirmation hearings to become the US health secretary, citing a report by the Guardian .
Ron Wyden of Oregon, the incoming chair of the powerful Senate finance committee, is seeking extensive records from Children’s Health Defense (CHD), the non-profit anti-vaccine group Kennedy has used as a vehicle to fuel his political rise, including all documents related to a 2019 trip Kennedy took to Samoa.
“We are beginning an investigation into evidence that Secretary of Health and Human Services Robert F Kennedy, Jr unlawfully lied to Congress on multiple occasions,” Wyden said in a letter to the group that was sent on Wednesday and obtained by the Guardian. The letter was also signed by Angela Alsobrooks, a Democratic senator from Maryland.
In the letter, the two lawmakers cited reporting by the Guardian that indicated Kennedy lied about his reasons for going to Samoa in 2019, a trip that occurred just months before a measles outbreak killed 83 people in the Pacific island nation, mostly children under age five.
The trip, which Kennedy made as the chair and chief legal counsel of CHD, became one of the most criticized events in his career before he entered government. Critics, including Samoan officials, have said Kennedy’s presence emboldened anti-vaccine activists in Samoa, worsening a vaccination crisis. Kennedy has denied the allegations, saying he never gave any public statement about vaccines or discouraged Samoans from getting vaccinated.
“We are deeply concerned by the tactics Kennedy has used – both before and during his tenure as secretary – to stand in the way of children receiving life-saving vaccinations,” the two Democratic senators wrote. “In Samoa and in the United States, unvaccinated children have died tragic and preventable deaths during measles outbreaks. We intend to hold Secretary Kennedy accountable for the grave harm he has caused to vulnerable children. We also intend to hold him accountable for any false statements made to Congress, a crime that undermines the Senate’s ability to fulfill its constitutional duties.”
In two congressional confirmation hearings in January 2025, Kennedy told lawmakers who held the key to his confirmation that his visit to Samoa had “nothing to do with vaccines”.
But letters obtained by the Guardian and the Associated Press through an open records lawsuit brought by the Reporters Committee for Freedom of the Press contradicted that testimony. In one he wrote to the Samoan prime minister in January 2019 before the trip, Kennedy explicitly said he wanted to study the measles, mumps and rubella (MMR) vaccine in the Pacific island nation. In it, he used the words “vaccine” or “vaccination” eight times.
The prime minister responded a month later , saying Samoa could benefit from CHD’s assessment of MMR vaccines and inviting him to come.
Children’s Health Defense did not respond to requests for comment, and the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) did not immediately comment.
HHS previously said in response to the Guardian’s reporting on Kennedy’s Senate testimony that his visit to Samoa was “unrelated to vaccines. Any claim or insinuation based on these letters that Secretary Kennedy lied under oath or to Congress is not only false but outright defamatory.” It has not provided a response to questions about why his testimony contradicted what he said in his letter to the Samoan prime minister.
By requesting documents from CHD, Wyden is aiming at the heart of Kennedy’s political machine. Since taking office, Kennedy has hired former CHD employees, including Lyn Redwood, a former CHD president who made early outreach on his behalf to Samoa . Redwood is now an employee at the HHS, reportedly working on vaccine safety . Kennedy’s closest adviser at HHS, Stefanie Spear, ran CHD’s newsletter before joining his 2024 presidential campaign.
With Kennedy now in government, CHD and its leaders often act as his most vociferous defenders, praising his work and explaining his decisions on their video podcasts, articles and on social media. Kennedy headlined CHD’s annual conference in September, where he made false and misleading claims about the safety of vaccines .
The Senate letter requested all documents related to any travel to Samoa by Kennedy or other employees or associates of CHD and any communications with Samoan government officials. It also asked for records related to Kennedy’s presidential campaign and his Senate confirmation process.
In addition, the senators requested records related to Kennedy’s speech to CHD’s September convention and all communications between CHD and federal government officials since 20 January 2025.
CHD has a deadline of 4 December.
On the night of the election, after polls closed and it became clear Democrats would take a majority of seats in the Senate, Wyden made a social media post with a direct message about accountability. “ Subpoenas ,” he wrote, in the one-word post. Alsobrooks, a member of the Senate committee on health, education, labor and pensions, has repeatedly called on Kennedy to resign or be fired .
The letter does not go as far as the legal force of a subpoena. But it would be a good idea to treat such a letter seriously, said Tim Stretton , of the Project on Government Oversight, a nonpartisan watchdog group in Washington.
“It’s not wise to ignore it,” Stretton said. “It’s really in their interest now to cooperate in a good faith effort.”
If they don’t, he said, the committee or chair could issue subpoenas to demand the information they are seeking.
Knowingly giving material false testimony to Congress is a crime that carries a possible prison sentence, though it is rarely prosecuted.
Wyden previously called for a criminal investigation of Kennedy’s testimony about his trip to Samoa. He said in August he would be pressing Republican colleagues to issue a criminal referral of Kennedy to the Department of Justice for a criminal investigation. He said then that “when Democrats retake the majority in the Senate, RFK will be at the top of the list of Trump officials the finance committee will hold accountable for endangering American families”.
Several other Democrats have called for Kennedy to resign or be impeached. Bernie Sanders, incoming chair of the Senate committee on health, education, labor and pensions, said he is open to impeachment . And the incoming senator Annie Andrews, a pediatrician from South Carolina, has been calling for Kennedy’s impeachment since her campaign.
Legal experts have said it is unlikely the justice department under Trump would prosecute, but said Kennedy’s statements could be used as grounds for hearings, for an impeachment inquiry or to create other obstacles for the Trump administration .

articles.title_orig: CoreWeave Stock Dives. It's in the Nvidia Danger Zone With These Other AI Plays.
articles.title_zh: CoreWeave Stock Dives. It's in the Nvidia Danger Zone With These Other AI Plays.
articles.content_orig:
The Nasdaq Composite fluctuated on Thursday as investors assessed the departure of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang , betting it would not derail the whole AI trade.
The tech-heavy Nasdaq was last down 0.3%, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average traded around the flatline. The S&P 500 fell 0.1%.
Selling pressure on Nvidia eased a bit, with the stock last down 5%. The shares were down double digits at one point after the company announced that Huang had resigned and named CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO. This comes after Huang reportedly had an affair with an alleged Chinese spy.
Investors moved into competitors of Nvidia, including Advanced Micro Devices and Broadcom , helping to bolster the market. AMD shares were up 4%, while Broadcom gained 5%.
Hyperscalers Microsoft and Alphabet — key buyers of Nvidia chips and leaders of the AI rally — also increased.
"This is a golden opportunity for Amazon, for Google, for AMD, for Broadcom, for OpenAI and Anthropic, who are hiring chip experts to help them design their own chips," said Jed Ellerbroek, portfolio manager at Argent Capital Management.
"Nvidia's fate as one company is one thing, but this AI revolution is way bigger than that," he also said. "If Nvidia falls from grace and their chips are no longer the best, and AMDs are better or Google's are better, then people will switch over and buy them. The demand for the chips is not is not going down."
There was a sense from investors that perhaps Huang's exit was a capitulation event for the AI trade with Nvidia's stock down by more than 25% the past one month as this scandal was unfolding.
"We are sticking with the thesis that technology stocks bottomed last week," said Tom Lee, the head of research at Fundstrat, in a note Thursday. Huang's departure "does not change our view."
Stocks outside of technology such as JPMorgan and Eli Lilly traded higher as well.
Stephanie Link said Thursday she sold her Nvidia following Jensen Huang's resignation from his post as CEO, with the investor moving into another artificial intelligence play: Micron Technology .
"The fundamentals are very, very strong at [Nvidia], and I expect the quarter next week to be very good with 300 billion in free cash flow next year," Link, the chief investment strategist at Hightower Advisors, said on CNBC's " Halftime Report ." "But, this stock is not going to trade on fundamentals ... for a while because you have the overhang of the investigations of leadership changes of potential departures."
CNBC Pro subscribers can read more here .
Nvidia shares were trading down 4% on Thursday after Jensen Huang announced he would immediately step down as CEO and a member of the board at the chipmaker.
The stock hovered just under $4 trillion in market cap, after paring steeper losses earlier in the day of more than 10%. Nvidia has closed above the market cap benchmark since July 2025.
Read the full story here .
Paul Meeks says he's buying Nvidia shares with "both hands" despite CEO Jensen Huang's resignation , because the decline amid this unfolding scandal has brought the stock down to "stupid" valuation levels.
The Freedom Capital head of technology research noted that the stock is trading at just 10 times fiscal 2028 earnings estimates after Thursday's decline.
Nvidia shares are off 20% in November alone, pressured by the scandal unfolding.
"I think that the actual announcement of his resignation is a market-clearing event," said Meeks.
CNBC Pro subscribers can learn more about Meeks' other key points here .
Even as Nvidia shares remained lower following CEO Jensen Huang's resignation , the broader market rose as investors moved past the announcement.
The S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite , both of which began Thursday's session lower, rose 0.2% and 0.1%, respectively.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average outperformed, rising 138 points, or 0.3%.
Sales of existing homes fell to their lowest level in more than 16 years during October, the National Association of Realtors reported Thursday.
A decline of 5.5% brought the seasonally adjusted annualized rate down to 3.75 million during a month that saw mortgage rates continue to climb, putting pressure on an already beleaguered housing market. The total was the lowest since August 2010.
"Home buying is difficult when mortgage rates have climbed to their highest levels since 2000, aside from a single month in 2023," said NAR chief economist Lawrence Yun. "Based on the current underwhelming home sales pace at a time of consistent job growth, there could be sizable pent-up demand if mortgage rates decline."
Nvidia shares are seeing huge volume as the stock drops following the resignation of CEO Jensen Huang .
The chipmaker saw more than 373 million shares traded amid the selling pressure. That's above the stock's 30-day average of 144.4 million.
The stock was last down more than 5%.
Cleveland Federal Reserve President Beth Hammack said Thursday she doesn't see the need for aggressive interest rate increases ahead.
While Hammack still supports rate hikes as the Fed struggles to get inflation back to its 2% target, she advocated for a gradual approach that the economy can adapt to more easily.
"I think we need to move rates higher to get to a restrictive stance of policy to bring inflation back down to 2%. My view is that if we go steadily in smaller increments, more frequent, smaller rises, it's easier for businesses and households to manage around that," she sad. "It's less disruptive to the overall economy than moving in sharper, more aggressive movements."
Earlier in the week, Fed Governor Christopher Waller raised the specter of a half-point hike at the December meeting if the inflation data comes in worse than anticipated. However, Hammack said she doesn't think that's necessary, at least for now.
"If we get behind the curve, and I don't think we're behind the curve today, but if we get behind the curve, then that might be something that we need to consider," she said. "So I'll certainly have an open mind walking into that December meeting."
The S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite began Thursday's session in the red.
The broad market index fell 0.8% shortly after the opening bell, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq declined 1.5%. The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 108 points, or 0.2%.
Shares of Broadcom and Advanced Micro Devices gained about 3% each in premarket trading after Jensen Huang resigned as CEO of Nvidia.
The company's chief financial officer Colette Kress has been named interim chief.
Nvidia shares were last down about 10%.
For more, follow along with our live updates of Nvidia and Jensen Huang here .
Initial jobless claims showed a modest pop last week after hovering around their lowest levels since the late 1960s.
First-time filings for unemployment benefits totaled a seasonally adjusted 200,000 for the week ending Nov. 7, a gain of 9,000 from the prior period and higher than the Dow Jones consensus for 195,000, the Labor Department reported Thursday.
Continuing claims, which run a week behind, fell 20,000 to just below 1.7 million.
Nebius shares plummeted in the premarket on Thursday after the neocloud's third-quarter revenue topped analysts' expectations, but its guidance disappointed investors.
The stock was last down almost 16%. That's after it rose more than 15% in Wednesday's regular session.

articles.title_orig: Ukraine peace talks: Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff conclude talks with Putin
articles.title_zh: Ukraine peace talks: Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff conclude talks with Putin
articles.content_orig:
Below is a roundup of developments from the Ukraine-Russia talks on Thursday, November 12:
US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff have concluded meetings with Russian President Vladimir Putin and will now travel to Dublin, Ireland, where they will meet with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy who is attending a European summit there.
Kushner, US President Donald Trump's son-in-law, described talks with Putin as "substantive and detailed."
He and Witkoff were in Moscow after two-days of talks in Abu Dhabi seeking to find a way to end Russia's ongoing invasion of Ukraine.
In Moscow, however, Putin showed no inclination toward compromise, saying that he would no back off of his territorial demands, while at the same time rejecting proposals to station foreign peacekeeping troops in  Ukraine, dismissing such a deployment as a "continuation of war."
US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner discussed their trip to Abu Dhabi this week with Russian President Vladimir Putin .
According to Russian state media RIA Novosti, Witkoff said US President Donald Trump was "seeking to end the conflict in Ukraine as quickly as possible."
The three-way talks in Abu Dhabi between the US, Ukraine and Russia were held "in a positive atmosphere" and that the Ukrainian and Russian delegations had "worked effectively," Ria Novosti reported.
Witkoff said he would convey the results of his and Kushner's meeting with Putin to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy .
Kushner, for his part, said the US had begun discussions with European countries on the post-war "security architecture" on the continent.
He also said Europe wanted to be involved in the talks to end the conflict, RIA Novosti reported.
Russian President Vladimir Putin has proposed a "humanitarian mission" to the frontline city of Kostyantynivka in eastern Ukraine, Russian state media reported.
Putin made the remarks during a meeting at the Kremlin on Thursday with US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, Ria Novosti said.
"There's a village in Donbas called Kostyantynivka, where there are still about 400-500 civilians. Let's do the same thing we did in Oleshky and invite representatives of the foreign press, including the American press," he said, referring to the recent US-brokered evacuation of the Russia-occupied city of Oleshky in southern Ukraine .
According to RIA Novosti, Putin also repeated Russia's demands in a potential peace deal, including its refusal to accept any foreign troops in Ukraine.
The Russian leader warned that international peacekeepers in Ukraine would become a "legitimate target for the Russian army."
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said the Russian side is becoming more willing to accept a European seat in the trilateral talks.
Merz said he expected Putin to agree to Europeans getting a seat at the table in talks with Ukraine. He was speaking on the sidelines of the European Political Community meeting in Dublin. He added that getting Putin to negotiate is more important than naming who would be the European envoy.
"The important thing is that Russia comes to the table and that Russia is ready to talk," the German chancellor said.
He also highlighted Ukraine's importance to Europe, saying that supporting Kyiv was a "shared European responsibility."
For some time, European leaders have sought a seat at the US-mediated Russia-Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi. So far, representatives from the EU were only present on the sidelines of the talks.
Ukraine's military said on Thursday it ‌has hit ⁠Russia's five ​largest oil ​refineries since ​October 30.
Those struck were the Omsk, Kirishi, Ryazan, Nizhny Novgorod and Yaroslavl refineries, along with the smaller Novokuibyshevsk and Saratov refineries, the General Staff said in a Telegram post.
The statement claimed that the strikes on key refining units are shrinking revenues that help Russia fund the war.
Referring to the Omsk refinery's distance of 2,500 kilometers (1,553 miles) from the Ukrainian border.
Last month, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said that military strikes on Russian energy infrastructure would resume, despite US President Donald Trump's insistence that such attacks stop.
Trump said Ukraine's strikes on Russian oil refineries were a "disgrace" and that Zelenskyy was less willing than Putin to reach a compromise to end the war.
Russia , however, has paid no heed to Trump, instead continuing to hit Ukraine's civilian energy infrastructure.
To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video
Leaders from more than 40 European countries will gather in the Irish capital Dublin on Thursday for the European Political Community summit to discuss the continent's security and Ukraine.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy will also attend the meeting, along with Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte.
US mediators, Jared Kushner, the son-in-law of US President Donald Trump , and special envoy Steve Witkoff are also expected to make their way to Ireland, after their meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow.
The meeting, due to begin at midday local time, is an opportunity for European leaders to discuss this week's trilateral peace talks between Ukraine, the US and Russia.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Thursday that Ukraine's military faced new "systematic restrictions" to tech billionaire Elon Musk's Starshield satellite internet.
"Our units have been recording significant disruptions to Starshield's operations over the territory of Ukraine for several days now," Zelenskyy said in an online post.
The Ukrainian president added that "systematic speed restrictions" were being imposed and that these are not "random errors."
"Unfortunately, this is helping the Russians kill more Ukrainians and carry out more accurate strikes against Ukraine."
The Starshield military communications system — the military-grade version of satellite-based communication network Starlink — is operated by Musk's SpaceX and plays a key role for frontline communications.
Ukraine first flagged issues with Starshield last month after a dispute between Zelenskyy and US President Donald Trump over a US deal allowing more Russian diesel into global markets.
The Wall Street Journal reported that Musk "capped the speeds at which Ukrainian hardware could stay connected to the satellite-based network."
Tech billionaire and US president both denied throttling Ukrainian access, but Musk later accused Ukraine of using the service for military purposes while Trump said Musk had "put it back."
Nearly half a million Russian soldiers may have been killed in Vladimir Putin 's war in Ukraine. Can Russia continue fighting at such an enormous human and economic cost?
Leaked records reportedly obtained from Russia's state statistics agency, Rosstat, identify more than 412,000 deaths linked to the war. British newspaper The Guardian reports that the true death toll could be closer to 500,000.
The full dataset has not been independently verified.
Some months saw more than 500 Russian soldiers killed every day. And the losses have fallen disproportionately on Russia's poorer and more remote regions.
In this DW News interview, Janis Kluge, head of the Eastern Europe and Eurasia research division at the German Institute for International and Security Affairs (SWP), examines what the leaked figures reveal about Russia's military losses, recruitment crisis and war economy.
The leaked data comes as US-mediated peace talks between Russia and Ukraine conclude in Abu Dhabi without a breakthrough on ending the war.
The two sides have agreed to a prisoner exchange, but fundamental disagreements remain. Could mounting Russian losses eventually force Putin to compromise, or make him even more determined to continue the war?

articles.title_orig: The new Apple TV 4K is great, but expensive
articles.title_zh: The new Apple TV 4K is great, but expensive
articles.content_orig:
The fourth-generation Apple TV 4K is pricey at $300, but its hands-free Siri, blazing A19 performance, and ad-free tvOS interface make it the best premium media streamer you can buy.
The fourth-generation Apple TV 4K finally adds hands-free Siri and gets a major speed boost from the iPhone 17's A19 chip. It also costs $299, $170 more than its 2022 predecessor. That's a steep jump, though nearly every media streamer has gotten pricier this year as component costs have climbed. What you get for the money is the fastest streamer I've tested, running tvOS, the cleanest and most polished streaming platform available, with none of the ads or pushy recommendations that clutter competitors' platforms . It's also a capable smart home hub with Matter support, a FaceTime machine that uses your iPhone as a webcam, and, with two pairs of HomePods, the heart of a wireless surround-sound system. Cheaper alternatives abound, but the fourth-generation Apple TV 4K is the best premium media streamer you can buy, earning it our Editors' Choice award.
I thought the $129 third-generation Apple TV 4K was too expensive when I reviewed it four years ago, so the new model's $300 price seemed absurd at first, even with its upgrades. Then I tested it, and its speed, hands-free Siri, and ad-free interface changed my mind.
Still, if $300 is more than you want to spend, there are strong alternatives. The Roku Ultra ($149.99) also offers hands-free voice control and a streamlined, media-forward interface, though it lacks a full AI assistant and the Apple TV 4K's extensive smart home features. The Amazon Fire TV Cube ($199.99) has hands-free Alexa+ and is an even more powerful smart home hub, but its interface is clunky and full of ads, and it doesn't support AirPlay. And if you don't need hands-free voice control at all, streaming sticks like the Amazon Fire TV Stick 4K Plus ($69.99) and the Roku Streaming Stick Plus ($59.99) add streaming to any TV for well under $100.
The new Apple TV 4K looks just like its predecessor: a black, rounded square box measuring 3.7 by 1.2 inches (width by height). The front has a status LED, and the back has HDMI, Ethernet, and power-cable ports.
The remote is also unchanged on the outside. It's a slim aluminum bar that feels more like a narrow iPhone than a typical streaming remote. Near the top is a large navigation pad with a circular center button that doubles as a touchpad. Above the pad sit the power button and a pinhole microphone, and a Siri button runs along the right edge. The rest of the controls are minimal: a volume rocker, a mute button, a play/pause button, a back button (long-press it to return to the home screen), and an Apple TV button, which opens the Apple TV app with a press and a quick settings menu with a long press. A built-in rechargeable battery charges over USB-C on the bottom.
The remote looks and feels great in the hand, but it can occasionally be frustrating to use. The touchpad is overly sensitive, and I’ve repeatedly brushed against it while pressing the directions around it, throwing off what I was trying to select. You can turn off the touchpad, but that raises the question of whether it was necessary to begin with. It can be useful when you want to swipe through multiple items at once, but I ended up turning it off anyway. I also kept mistaking the Apple TV button for the Home button until I found a setting that made it one. With those two tweaks, the remote became much easier to use.
Internally, the remote has a new trick: Precision Finding. If you have an iPhone 17 or later, an iPhone Air , or an iPhone Duo , you can use the Find My app to locate the remote to within about two feet. You can also use your phone to activate a chime on the remote to find it more easily.
The Apple TV 4K gets a major hardware boost from the A19 chip, the same processor that powers the iPhone 17 , along with 8GB of memory. That's a big jump from the previous model's A15 Bionic (from the iPhone 13 ) and 4GB of memory. Media streamers don't need nearly as much processing power as phones or tablets, but extra headroom makes them more responsive when you jump between apps or play 4K HDR content. It also makes the Apple TV 4K a better gaming machine, since dozens of Apple Arcade titles run on tvOS.
Wireless connectivity also gets a bump on the new Apple TV 4K. It has Wi-Fi 7 , enabling 6GHz band connections and future-proofing it considerably compared with the third-generation’s Wi-Fi 6. Gigabit Ethernet is built-in if you want a wired network link. It also features Bluetooth 6.0 compared with the previous model’s Bluetooth 5.0.
For all that new tech, the fourth-generation Apple TV 4K’s media capabilities are the same as its predecessor's. It plays 4K video, including high dynamic range ( HDR ) content in Dolby Vision, HDR10, and HDR10+, and supports Dolby Atmos spatial audio . That covers just about every format you'll encounter.
Speaking of spatial audio, the Apple TV 4K has a neat new trick if you own second-generation HomePods or HomePod mini 2s . Earlier models let you connect a stereo pair of HomePods, which already sounds better than most TV speakers. The fourth-generation model lets you add a second pair, placing four HomePods as front-left, front-right, rear-left, and rear-right speakers for surround sound. With HomePod minis, you get 4.0-channel surround. With full-size HomePods, whose multiple directional drivers can bounce sound around the room, you get a full spatial audio sound field, including height effects.
It's similar to Fire TV's Alexa Home Theater , which pairs multiple Echo Dot Max or Echo Studio speakers with a compatible Fire TV device. I'm still testing the feature and will cover it in more detail in a separate story, but so far, setup has been smooth.
For the first few iterations of the Apple TV, I lamented its limited selection of apps and services, but the device has come a long way in recent years. Apple has polished its tvOS platform to a shine, making for an impressively elegant, smooth, and full-featured media streaming experience.
The interface is built around big, friendly tiles, with a simple home screen that holds six apps in a macOS dock-like bar at the bottom, and a larger contextual view that shows art or content suggestions based solely on the selected app. Scrolling down brings you to the full selection of apps on the device, and you can organize them into folders. It’s easy to understand, simple to navigate, and has no ads whatsoever. It’s everything I like about Roku’s devices, but even more polished.
For streaming, tvOS covers all major services including Apple TV (obviously), Amazon Prime Video , Crunchyroll, Disney+, Netflix, Twitch, and YouTube. You can also mirror your iPhone, iPad, or Mac screen to it over AirPlay. For local media servers, Plex has an official tvOS app, while Emby and Jellyfin have a slew of third-party apps but no official ones; I had no problem connecting to my Jellyfin server with several of them.
I want to give particular credit to the Twitch app on tvOS as the most responsive version I’ve used on a media streamer. On multiple Fire TV and Google TV devices I've tested, the Twitch app lags several seconds when backing out of a channel to the main app screen. On the Apple TV 4K, it’s instant. It's a small thing, but as a Twitch watcher, I appreciate it.
If you like to game, you can pair a Bluetooth gamepad to the Apple TV 4K to play. The selection is overwhelmingly mobile-focused, with the same kinds of games you would find on iPad, but there are still some great console-like picks like Dead Cells, PowerWash Simulator, and SpongeBob SquarePants: Battle for Bikini Bottom.
Apple Arcade extends to tvOS, too, though I didn’t see many stand-out gamepad games on it besides the aforementioned PowerWash Simulator. A Steam Link client is also available, so you can stream games from your PC to your TV. Thanks to the A19 chip, games play very smoothly.
